**This is the document the code is written from.**

Eight lanes wrote the eight epics independently and blind, each reading the same frozen
sources, the same BRD rows and the same records, with no sight of another lane's draft. The

# S1 — Reading rules and the provenance grammar

```
Document .......... docs/03 PRD/FrontRow_PRD.md
Derived from ...... SRC-001 + its §E (ten errata) · SRC-002 + its §E (six errata)
                    SRC-003 (client rulings, 2026-08-14, forty rows)
                    docs/02 BRD/FrontRow_BRD.md (ninety-three R-rows)
                    the seventy-three APPROVED records in docs/01 ADR/all-ADRs/
                    docs/05 B DesignSystem/ (tokens.css, COMPONENTS.md, DESIGN-SYSTEM.md)
Written ........... 2026-08-14
Constitution ...... frontrow-constitution@0.1.0
Authority ......... CONSTITUTION.md Art II.1. Where this document and a frozen source
                    disagree, the frozen source wins and this document is the defect.
```

> **This is the document the code is written from.** The BRD says what the business needs; this says
> what the system does about it. A developer with this document, the design system and the data model
> should not have to guess.
>
> Where they would have to guess, that is a defect in this document — and the count of such places was
> measured by a fresh reader who had seen nothing else. `S8.6` reports it.

## S1.1 How a specification row is shaped

Every product specification is one row with a fixed shape and a fixed id, `P-XXX-nn`:

```
### `P-XXX-nn` · a short imperative name · STATUS
[SRC: the clause, ruling or record it comes from]
[BRD: the business requirement row it satisfies]

Behaviour · Who may do it · Preconditions · Happy path ·
Exception paths (every one, with the exact words the user sees) ·
Server-side validation · Worked example where it computes a number
```

**A row with no `[SRC:]` tag is a defect. A row with no `[BRD:]` tag is a defect.** Nothing in this
document is here because it seemed sensible. The two tags answer two different questions: `[SRC:]`
says *what authority permits this*, `[BRD:]` says *which business need it discharges*. A row can
resolve one and fail the other, so both are checked, in both directions (`S8.1`).

### The prefixes

| Prefix | Epic | Section |
|---|---|---|
| `P-SCP` | scope and the exclusions carried from the BRD | `S2` |
| `P-BRW` | browse and discover | `S4 / E1` |
| `P-SEA` · `P-HLD` | the seat map's interactive behaviour, and the hold | `S4 / E2` |
| `P-PAY` | checkout, money and payment | `S4 / E3` |
| `P-TKT` | the receipt, the reference and entry | `S4 / E4` |
| `P-ACC` | accounts and the customer's own bookings | `S4 / E5` |
| `P-ADM` | admin: movies, showtimes, pricing, halls | `S4 / E6` |
| `P-RPT` | the manager and admin dashboard | `S4 / E7` |
| `P-XCT` | cross-cutting floors | `S4 / E8` and `S7` |

Screens are `SCR-XXX-nn` (`S5`). Endpoints are `EP-XXX-nn` (`S6`).

**One variance, stated rather than left to be noticed.** The `P-SCP` rows in `S2` describe things that
are **not built**. They carry `[SRC:]`, `[BRD:]`, a statement of what is not built, what the system
does instead, and — because `SRC-001 §6.6` binds — **what keeps it possible later**. They have no
happy path, because there is no path.

## S1.2 Precedence — which statement wins when two places say the same thing

**This document states many facts more than once, and that is the defect class it has produced most.**
Eight lanes wrote it independently; the overlaps are where they restate each other, and a restatement
that drifts is invisible to every mechanical check, because both copies resolve, both cite correctly
and both are internally consistent.

Naming the instances has been done four times. **This is the rule that makes the next one resolvable
without a fifth pass.**

| Rank | The authority | For |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the **`endpoint` block** in `S6` | **wire shape**: the path, the method, parameter and field names, their types and bounds, and the HTTP status of every response. `api/contract.json` is generated from these blocks, so a P-row disagreeing with one is disagreeing with the artefact the client and the server are both built from |
| 2 | the **P-row that owns the behaviour** | **behaviour, and the exact words the customer reads.** Ownership is stated on the row. Where a row says it is "the complete message set" for a code, no other section may publish a different string for that code |
| 3 | the **`SCR-` screen spec** | **layout, states and design tokens** — what renders, in which state, from which token |
| 4 | any **other passage that restates any of the above** | nothing. **A restatement carries no authority at all**, and where it differs from its owner it is a defect in the restatement, never in the owner |

**Three consequences, stated so they can be applied without judgement:**

- **A P-row and an `endpoint` block disagreeing about a status code or a field bound is resolved in
  favour of the block**, and the P-row is corrected. This is not a preference — the contract is
  generated from the block, so the block is what will exist.
- **An `endpoint` block and a P-row disagreeing about *behaviour* is resolved in favour of the
  P-row.** A block describes a shape; it does not decide what the system does.
- **A section that needs a fact it does not own should cite the owner rather than repeat it.** Every
  repetition is a copy that can go stale, and this document has proved that four times.

**Where ownership is not obvious it is declared.** The customer-facing message set for the hold codes
is owned by `P-HLD-14`; the seat-lifecycle behaviour by `P-SEA-06`'s state machine; the audit `action`
vocabulary by `P-ADM-19`; the configuration inventory by `S7.9`; the date and time rendering rule by
`S7.19`; **the duration and `Retry-After` rendering rule, and the derivation of every bucket's wait,
by `S7.20`**; **the rule that a number in customer copy which is configuration is rendered and never
typed, by `S7.21`**; the seat map's dependency-failure string by `P-BRW-12`; the error-code registry by
`api/error_codes.md`, which is generated and is **reproduced in `S6.0`** so that a reader holding
only this document can consult it. **Each of those says so on itself.**

`S7.20` and `S7.21` were added to this list after a reader pointed out that neither was on it. Every
lane had been corrected against `S7.20`, and on a literal reading of the ranking a rank-2 P-row still
outranked it — which would have un-corrected them all. **A rule that everything defers to belongs on
the list of things that own something**, and the omission is the kind this list exists to prevent.
Both sections declare the ownership on themselves, which is what made the omission findable.

### S1.2.1 Eight cases the ranking alone does not settle

The ranking orders *kinds of passage*. Eight situations need a rule of their own, and each was found
by a reader applying `S1.2` and reaching a case it did not reach.

**1. Two rank-2 rows, neither claiming ownership.** Two P-rows can both be about one behaviour with
neither declaring it owns the behaviour — the whole cross-cutting lane is structurally a set of rows
that restate other lanes' rows. **The rule: the row that specifies the behaviour in its own epic owns
it; a cross-cutting row that describes the same behaviour as a floor is a restatement and is rank 4.**
Where that is still ambiguous, **ownership is declared explicitly on the owning row** in the form
`P-HLD-14` uses, and the list above is extended. A tie that survives both of those is a defect to
raise, not a judgement for the implementer.

**2. A disagreement about existence, not value.** Rank 1 can define a shape that **cannot carry** what
rank 2 requires the client to do — a P-row demanding a state the endpoint's enum does not contain, or
a screen rendering a figure no response returns. Obeying both is impossible, so "the block wins on
shape, the row wins on behaviour" resolves nothing. **The rule: this is a defect in the pair, and it
stops.** It is not resolved by dropping the behaviour or by inventing the field — the shape is
corrected so it can carry the behaviour, and if that cannot be done without a decision nobody has
made, it becomes a `PROPOSED-` row.

**3. Where a `SCR-` row's copy stands.** Rank 3 is defined as layout, states and tokens — copy is not
in that list — yet every screen spec carries a copy table, and for some strings the screen is the only
place the string appears. **The rule: a `SCR-` row owns a customer-facing string when no P-row
publishes it, and never otherwise.** Where a P-row publishes the string, the screen renders it and may
not vary it; where no P-row does, the screen is the source and the string is as binding as any other.
A screen may never overrule a P-row on wording — that would invert rank 2.

**4. A rank-2 row says a capability exists and the rank-3 screen draws no control for it.** Rank 3 is
"what renders", which is the axis in dispute, so the ranking argues with itself. **The rule: behaviour
outranks rendering on whether a capability exists.** If a P-row says the admin does something, the
screen gains the control; the screen may decide how it looks and where it sits, never whether it is
there. Note what this does *not* license: it does not let a P-row invent copy for the control it just
created — case 3 still governs the strings, so the screen publishes them.

Two rows were built on this in the iteration-6 fix pass and each states the tie-break at its own site.
`P-ADM-07` says the admin optionally chooses a format and calls itself the only writer of
`showtime.format_id`, while `SCR-ADM-03` drew no format control — so `format_id` could never be set,
and the customer's format filter could never render. `P-ADM-24`'s happy path opens "the admin opens
the vocabulary on `SCR-ADM-07` and withdraws an entry", while `SCR-ADM-07` drew no withdraw control —
so `EP-ADM-27` was unreachable from the product and eight audit actions were unwritable. **In both,
the screen was missing something rather than disagreeing about it**, which is the tell for this case:
a screen that contradicts a P-row is case 2, a screen that is silent where a P-row acts is case 4.

**5. The generated error-code registry against a block or a row.** `S1.2` names the registry as an
owner and never ranks it, which leaves a three-way tie: an endpoint block declaring a status, a P-row
declaring a code, and `api/error_codes.md` pairing that code with a different status. **The rule: the
generated registry fixes a code's status, and neither a block nor a row may contradict it.** A code
means one thing on the wire or it means nothing — a client branches on `code` (`FR-ADR-052`), and a
code that arrives with two different statuses is two codes wearing one name.

The registry is generated, so this is not a fourth authority competing with the other three: it is the
adjudicated union of the `newerrorcode` blocks the lanes raised, and **the way to change it is to
raise one**, never to write a different pairing into a block. `P-ADM-17` and `EP-ADM-24` were the case
that found this — both said `409 VALIDATION_FAILED`, a pairing that does not exist, because the
registry fixes `VALIDATION_FAILED` at `422`. Both were corrected to `422`; no new code was minted,
because an existing one covered the case.

**6. Two rank-3 screens covering one surface.** The ranking places every `SCR-` row at rank 3, so it
cannot separate two of them — and two do collide, because some screens are **cross-cutting
registries** that publish a string or a control for a *code* across the whole product, while others
own *one surface* and publish for that surface. When they disagree, the ranking has nothing to say.
**The rule: the screen that owns the surface wins, and the cross-cutting registry defers to it by
name for that surface.** The registry keeps its entry as the rule everywhere else — it is not deleted
and it is not narrowed to nothing, because the whole point of a registry is that a code not
specifically claimed still has an answer.

`SCR-XCT-01` and `SCR-SEA-03` were the pair that found this: the registry published a
`Choose seats again` banner action for `HOLD_EXPIRED`, and the seat map said
`DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` is the only code there that carries a control. The seat map is right about
its own surface for a reason the registry could not have known — **a customer meeting `HOLD_EXPIRED`
on the seat map is already on the screen that button would send them to**, so the control navigates
nowhere. That asymmetry is why the surface owner wins: the registry knows the code, the surface knows
the situation.

**7. A step list is silent about a write a declared cross-lane owner requires.** A P-row's happy path
is written as an exhaustive ordered procedure — step 1 through step *n* — and **the exhaustive form
makes a silence read as a decision.** When another row **declares ownership** of some effect and says
it happens during that procedure, the step list's silence is not a disagreement the ranking can
settle: both rows are rank 2, both are declared owners of different things, and nothing about the
shape prevents either. **The rule: an ordered step list is authoritative on ordering and is never
authoritative on completeness.** A declared owner elsewhere adds its write to the list; the step list
does not remove it by omission. **The fix is to add the step**, so the procedure is exhaustive in
fact and not only in form.

This case has now been found twice, which is why it is a rule and not a correction. `P-PAY-10`'s
confirm transaction listed eleven steps and a sixteen-row crash table and never mentioned the
`receipt_dispatch` insert that `P-TKT-04` says happens inside it — build it from its owning row alone
and **no receipt is ever sent**. `P-HLD-01` and `P-HLD-08` list the hold and release procedures and
never mention the seat-map cache `DEL` that `P-BRW-12` — the declared owner of seat-map invalidation
— requires after both. The consequence there is smaller and still observable: the live seat map moves
in about three seconds or in about thirteen, on the one screen the product is about.

**Both were found by readers, not by the checks**, and that is the point worth keeping: a missing step
resolves cleanly, produces no contradiction a grep can find, and every gate stays green.

**8. One owning row that contradicts itself.** The ranking compares passages of different kinds, so
it has nothing to say when **a single row, declared owner of a thing, states it two ways.** There is
no second passage to outrank. **The rule: a declared owner that contradicts itself is a defect in
that row and it stops — the reader may not pick the half they prefer, and may not resolve it by
looking for a third passage elsewhere.** The fix is that the owning row states the thing once.

`P-BRW-04` was the case. It declares itself the owner of the listing's date strip and says the strip
runs *"through the latest `display_until`"* — and also that it is *"`P-BRW-06`'s rule with a maximum
applied"*, where `P-BRW-06` says the strip runs to **the day before** `display_until`, because that
value is an exclusive bound. **One day apart, in one row, about the row's own subject.** A reader
taking the first reading renders one extra day button whose only possible result is the empty state
the same row says must never be reached.

**The tell for this case is that both halves sound like the rule rather than like a restatement**,
which is what stops the ranking from firing. `S1.2` is built to compare a rule against a copy of it;
here there is no copy.

**A note on how many of these there now are.** Eight cases is more than a ranking should need, and
each was added only after a reader hit it and could not proceed. They are not refinements of the rule
— they are the places the rule does not reach, written down rather than left for the next reader to
rediscover. **If a ninth is found, add it; do not reword the ranking to pretend it covered the
case.**

## S1.2a The four citations that are permitted, and no others

| Citation | Means |
|---|---|
| `SRC-001 §n` | the client's product requirement, frozen 2026-08-14 |
| `SRC-002 §n` | the client's build mandate, frozen 2026-08-14 |
| `SRC-003 <ROW-ID>` | the client's own ruling of 2026-08-14 — the newest and most authoritative |
| `FR-ADR-nnn` | an `APPROVED` record in `docs/01 ADR/all-ADRs/`, governed by the ledger |

Every citation in this document resolves. `py tools/consistency_check.py` checks it mechanically and
its output is pasted in `S8.2` rather than claimed.

**The seventy-three records are `APPROVED` and immutable** (`CONSTITUTION.md` Art III.3). This
document never re-opens one. Where it appears to go further than a record, it is specifying the
record's consequence, not amending it.

## S1.3 Sixteen clauses are withdrawn or corrected — a spec derived from one is a defect

`SRC-003` filed **ten errata against `SRC-001` and six against `SRC-002`**. Twelve clauses of
`SRC-001 §1`–`§9` are withdrawn outright, one is corrected, and **the whole of `SRC-002 §10` is
withdrawn**. BRD `B7.3` lists every one.

The five that most often produce a wrong specification, listed here because a reader who skips `B7.3`
will otherwise write one of them:

| Clause | Erratum | What a defect derived from it looks like |
|---|---|---|
| `SRC-001 §5.6` and `SRC-002 §10` — the external movie source | withdrawn, `SRC-001 §E E-4` / `SRC-002 §E E-2` | any import, any upsert-by-external-id, any "source unavailable" path, any attribution footer |
| `SRC-002 §4.6` — a scheduler; `SRC-002 §8.1.1` — a seven-minute hold | withdrawn / corrected, `SRC-002 §E E-4` / `§E E-1` | any scheduled job at all; **any document stating seven minutes** |
| `SRC-001 §5.3.3` and `SRC-002 §8.5.1` — a scannable ticket | corrected, `SRC-001 §E E-9` / `SRC-002 §E E-5` | a QR code, a scanner, a validation endpoint, a used-ticket state |
| `SRC-001 §5.4.3` — cancel a booking | withdrawn, `SRC-001 §E E-2` | a cancellation control, a refund, a cancellation policy |
| `SRC-001 §9.5` — a third-party payment provider | withdrawn, `SRC-001 §E E-10` | any provider integration, any card field, any card-shaped fixture |

**Three clauses of `CONSTITUTION.md` are stale** and are not inherited here: Art I.6 (the win
condition still describes a scannable ticket and a scheduled import), Art V.8 (refunds described as
open when both were ruled), Art VIII.13 (the outbound list still names the withdrawn movie source).
`SRC-003` and the errata win under Art II.1. **The corrected win condition is BRD `B3.3`** and it is
carried into `S2.1`. Amending the Constitution is reserved to the client (Art XII.1), so this is
raised, not fixed.

## S1.4 Status law — the rule that matters most in this document

| Status | Meaning here |
|---|---|
| `RULED` | decided, with a citation to a frozen source or an `APPROVED` record |
| `PROVISIONAL` | a build-session reading that reconciles two of the client's own answers. **One message from the client reverses it.** It never reads as settled fact |
| `ASSUMED` | the client said "you pick". It is the build session's choice and **it never hardens into a requirement** |
| `OPEN` | genuinely unruled. It is named, never filled in. **Escalate, never invent** |

### The three `PROVISIONAL` readings, and where each bites

| Reading | Rejected alternative | Where it bites in this document |
|---|---|---|
| **Four roles**, not one (`SRC-003 C-1`, `FR-ADR-009`) | three roles, the dashboard served to admins filtered by hall | `S3`, every `P-RPT` row, every authorisation rule in `S6` |
| **One cinema with six screens** (`C-2`, `FR-ADR-010`) | several cinemas, as `SRC-001 §1.1` implies | the cinema filter's non-rendering, manager scoping attaching to the screen |
| **Sales close 15 minutes *after* the advertised start** (`OPEN-BOOK-03`, `FR-ADR-042`) | 15 minutes *before* — **half an hour apart** | every cut-off check, the closed-showtime state, the paying-past-the-cut-off edge |

### The three `ASSUMED` subjects

| Subject | The choice | The ruling |
|---|---|---|
| Hall sizes | 90 / 120 / 150 / 180 / 200 / 220 seats | "pick random" (`OPEN-SCALE-02`) |
| Peak concurrency | 50 simultaneous bookers, for the load test only | "you pick" (`OPEN-SCALE-03`) |
| Seat category names | Standard, Premium, Recliner | "you pick" (`OPEN-SEAT-01`) |

**None of the three is a requirement.** No design in this document may depend on a hall being exactly
220 seats, on there being exactly three categories, or on fifty being the real peak. The
correctness gate — exactly one winner for one seat — is **separate and is not assumed**
(`FR-ADR-034`).

### The four `OPEN` rows — named, never filled in

| Row | What this document specifies | What it must not |
|---|---|---|
| `OPEN-EMAILFAIL-01` | the surface: the reference on screen and in the bookings list independently of the email, the send state the booking record holds, the retry and dead-letter path | **any wording a customer whose receipt definitively failed would read, and any policy about money already taken** |
| `OPEN-SHOWCANCEL-01` | that **no withdraw-showtime capability exists in v1**, stated to the client rather than left to be found | any withdrawal endpoint, screen, refund or notification |
| `OPEN-ATTRIB-01` | that demonstration content is obviously demonstration content | any real title, poster, brand or source |
| `OPEN-TLS-01` | that `COOKIE_SECURE` is environment-driven and off in the deployed environment, and that the environment is never called production | that TLS is or will be terminated anywhere |

**An `OPEN` row filled in with something plausible is the cardinal failure of this project**
(`CONSTITUTION.md` Art VII.3). This project has already produced the milder version of it once: an
assumption of seven minutes in a question became a specification in the next document, and when it was
finally put to the client it came back as three.

## S1.5 Numbers, and why every one of them is worked through

`CONSTITUTION.md` Art IX.4: **every rule that computes a number states the rule, its inputs, and a
worked example with the expected answer.** A specification that computes money or time and gives no
worked example cannot produce a binary acceptance criterion, and "the seat map works" is not one
(Art IX.3).

Every worked example in this document is written so a test can be transcribed from it directly:
integer paise, ISO-8601 instants in both UTC and Asia/Kolkata, and the arithmetic shown rather than
the result asserted.

**A count stated in prose is a claim, and it is derived or it is wrong.** Every count in `S8` is
machine-derived by `docs/03 PRD/api/generate_api.py`, and the command that produced it is printed
next to it. This document states no figure it did not compute.

## S1.6 What is GENERATED, and what that buys

| File | Generated by | Checked how |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/03 PRD/api/contract.json` | `docs/03 PRD/api/generate_api.py` | regenerate and diff — **byte-identical or it fails** |
| `docs/03 PRD/api/error_codes.md` | the same | the same |

`CONSTITUTION.md` Art II.6 is the reason: a hash proves a file was not edited, but it cannot see a
requirement the file never contained. Where a document is marked GENERATED, the stronger check
regenerates it and compares content. **Never hand-edit either file.**

The generator's source is the `endpoint` blocks in `S6`. That is deliberate: it makes the API
contract a consequence of the specification rather than a parallel document that drifts from it.

## S1.7 Register

`SRC-002 §2` is a requirement on this document and not a courtesy. Everything here is written at the
level of someone who can code but has never run production infrastructure. **No analogies, no
metaphors, no figures of speech.** Short paragraphs.

Two consequences the client asked for by name:

- **When something will not fit in 1 GB, it is said, with the number** (`§13.6`), rather than quietly
  worked around. `S7` carries the memory figures and labels every one an estimate.
- **This product has never been observed running in AWS.** Every statement about its behaviour there
  is **reasoned, not observed**, and is labelled that way wherever it appears.

## S1.8 How this document was written, and why that matters

Eight lanes wrote the eight epics **independently and blind**, each reading the same frozen sources,
the same BRD rows and the same records, with no sight of another lane's draft. They were then merged,
and the merge pass hunted contradictions **between** lanes.

That is the defect class this stage exists to catch. Two sections that each resolve perfectly well on
their own and contradict each other are invisible to the mechanical checker (`Art IX.6`), and lanes
that can see each other converge — which makes the disagreement, the thing that carries the signal,
disappear. **Zero contradictions would have been a suspicious result, not a good one.** `S8.5` lists
what was found and how each was resolved.

`CONSTITUTION.md` Art VII.7 — the writer never verifies its own work — is discharged by a fresh
zero-context session that read only this document and reported every place it would have had to guess.
**That substitution is recorded rather than passed off as independent review**, and the count is in
`S8.6`, per iteration and not only at the end.

# S2 — Scope, carried from the frozen BRD

The BRD decided what the business needs. This section carries that boundary into the specification
without re-deciding any of it, and turns each exclusion into a row a reviewer can check.

---

## S2.1 The win condition, corrected

> `CONSTITUTION.md` Art I.6 still describes **a scannable ticket** and **movie data arriving from an
> external source on a schedule**. Both were withdrawn on 2026-08-14. Amending the Constitution is
> reserved to the client (Art XII.1), so the stale clause is raised and not edited. **This is the
> corrected win condition, taken from BRD `B3.3`.**

`[SRC: SRC-003 OPEN-ROLE-01 · SRC-003 OPEN-HOLD-01 · SRC-003 OPEN-PAY-01 · SRC-003 OPEN-TICKET-01 ·
SRC-003 OPEN-TMDB-01 · SRC-003 OPEN-SCOPE-01 · SRC-001 §3.2 · FR-ADR-006 · FR-ADR-034]`

A visitor browses the movies currently showing, registers, picks a showtime, sees a live seat map,
holds seats for three minutes, pays through the simulated payment step, and receives an **emailed
receipt carrying a unique booking reference**; **fifty simultaneous attempts on one seat produce
exactly one winner, proved in the database and not in the website's answer**; an **admin creates a
movie by hand** and it appears to customers; a **manager sees their own halls' numbers and nobody
else's**; and it runs on AWS from containers the client deployed by hand.

**Everything past that line is fast-follow.** Define victory, then stop.

## S2.2 The five success criteria, as this document must make testable

| # | Criterion | Where it becomes binary | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SC-1` | a signed-in customer completes a booking in under two minutes, seat map to confirmation. **A first-time visitor's run includes registration and will not meet it** — that figure is measured and reported separately, not quietly excluded | `P-ACC-06` | `SRC-001 §3.1` · `FR-ADR-046` |
| `SC-2` | **zero double-booked seats under concurrent load.** Fifty simultaneous attempts on one seat: **exactly one 201**, forty-nine `SEAT_UNAVAILABLE` 409s, one owner in the database. (201, not 200 — `EP-HLD-01` creates a hold. `CONSTITUTION.md` Art IX.3's illustrative "one 200" is an example of the *shape* of a binary criterion, not this endpoint's status.) **Not "at most one" — zero winners is also a failure.** Then the guard is dropped on purpose, watched failing, restored and verified | `P-HLD-13` | `SRC-001 §3.2` · `§2.2` · `§7.1` · `FR-ADR-024` · `FR-ADR-034` |
| `SC-3` | seat availability is accurate within a few seconds — **worst case about thirteen seconds**, stated rather than rounded down. Being out of date never causes a double sale | `P-BRW-09`, `S7.6` | `SRC-001 §3.3` · `§7.3` · `FR-ADR-030` |
| `SC-4` | **withdrawn.** `SRC-001 §3.4` was withdrawn by erratum `E-7`. There is no automatic listing update to measure | — | `SRC-001 §E E-7` |
| `SC-5` | a manager reads their own halls' occupancy for a chosen day, week or month, with no request to anyone | `P-RPT-01`, `P-RPT-04` | `SRC-001 §3.5` · `SRC-003 OPEN-REPORT-01` · `FR-ADR-043` |

**`SC-2` is never waived.** Waiving any quality check is reserved to the client (Art III.8), and
adopting a stricter option is not a waiver and needs no signature (Art III.10).

## S2.3 The eight phases, and what closes each

`[SRC: SRC-002 §12 · SRC-002 §12.1 · SRC-002 §E E-3 · SRC-003 OPEN-SCOPE-01 · FR-ADR-006]`

| Phase | What ships | Closes when |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | skeleton, config loading, health endpoints, structured logging, local `docker-compose` | the client has deployed it to ECS and been told what to test |
| 2 | data model, migrations, seed data, admin CRUD for halls, showtimes and pricing | the admin can configure a hall and price a showtime |
| 3 | public browsing, listings, the seat-map read path, caching | a guest can reach a live seat map |
| 4 | seat locking, booking confirmation, idempotency, **the concurrency proof** | `SC-2` is green **and the red-proof drill has been watched** |
| 5 | the SQS worker and the receipt email | a receipt arrives carrying a reference |
| 6 | **admin movie management** *(this replaced the withdrawn automatic import)* | an admin authors a movie by hand and a customer sees it |
| 7 | metrics, rate limiting, the load test, the runbook | the client can run the load test themselves |
| 8 | **the manager and admin dashboard** *(new, added by `SRC-003`)* | a manager sees their own halls and is denied another's |

**A phase closes only when the client has been told what to test** (`SRC-002 §12.1`). Every P-row in
this document names its phase.

## S2.4 What is not built

Eighteen rows, one per BRD `R-OUT` row. **Excluded is not blocked** (`SRC-001 §6.6`): no row here may
harden into something the business can never add, and each says what keeps it possible.

---

### `P-SCP-01` · No native mobile application · `RULED`
`[SRC: SRC-001 §6.1 · FR-ADR-044]`
`[BRD: R-OUT-01]`

**Not built.** No iOS or Android application, no app-store artefact, no native wrapper.

**What the system does instead.** One responsive web interface, designed and tested at the hardest
case it has: **the largest hall's seat map on a 375-pixel-wide screen** (`S7.13`). The client stated
the substitute themselves — "a website that works well on a phone is enough".

**What keeps it possible.** The interface is a separate static container talking to a JSON API over
`/api` (`S6`). A native client would consume the same contract. Nothing in the API assumes a browser.

**Phase.** n/a.

---

### `P-SCP-02` · No food and beverage ordering · `RULED`
`[SRC: SRC-001 §6.2]`
`[BRD: R-OUT-02]`

**Not built.** No concessions catalogue, no add-to-order, no non-ticket line on any total.

**What the system does instead.** A booking's amount is the sum of its seat prices and nothing else
(`P-PAY-07`). The stored total is a single figure.

**What keeps it possible.** Nothing in the money path forbids a second kind of line item later — but
note the constraint this creates: **the stored total cannot be split retrospectively**, because
nothing records what portion was ever meant to be what. Adding an order line later means adding it
going forward, not reinterpreting history. Recorded so it is a known limit rather than a discovery.

**Phase.** n/a.

---

### `P-SCP-03` · No loyalty points and no membership tiers · `RULED`
`[SRC: SRC-001 §6.3]`
`[BRD: R-OUT-03]`

**Not built.** No points balance, no tier on a user, no earn or burn, no member price.

**What the system does instead.** Every customer is priced identically: base price plus the category
uplift, uniform across every hall and every show (`P-PAY-05`).

**What keeps it possible.** The user row and the price computation are separate; a tier would be a
new input to one function (`FR-ADR-038`), not a second pricing path.

**Phase.** n/a.

---

### `P-SCP-04` · No multi-language interface · `RULED`
`[SRC: SRC-001 §6.4 · FR-ADR-044]`
`[BRD: R-OUT-04]`

**Not built.** No locale switch, no translation layer, no per-user language preference.

**What the system does instead.** One interface language. Movies still carry a `language` field
because it is something a customer filters on (`P-BRW-03`) — **that is the film's language, not the
interface's**, and the two are unrelated.

**What keeps it possible.** No user-facing string is assembled from fragments or interpolated
mid-sentence, so extracting them later is mechanical rather than a rewrite.

**Phase.** n/a.

---

### `P-SCP-05` · No point-of-sale integration · `RULED`
`[SRC: SRC-001 §6.5]`
`[BRD: R-OUT-05]`

**Not built.** No connection to any counter system, no import or export of counter sales, no shared
inventory with a till.

**What the system does instead.** Seats sold online are the only seats this system knows about. **A
seat sold at the counter is invisible to it**, and the seat map will show that seat as available.
Stated plainly because it is a real operational consequence: while both channels exist, the online map
is authoritative only for online sales.

**What keeps it possible.** The booking table already carries an owner and a source-agnostic seat
occupancy row; a counter sale would be another writer against the same unique constraint on
`(showtime_id, seat_id)`, which is what makes it safe to add.

**Phase.** n/a.

---

### `P-SCP-06` · No external source of film information, and no automatic import · `RULED`
`[SRC: SRC-003 OPEN-TMDB-01 · SRC-001 §E E-4 · SRC-002 §E E-2 · FR-ADR-006]`
`[BRD: R-OUT-06]`

**Not built.** No external movie API, no API key, no `region` parameter, no rate-limit backoff, no
upsert-by-external-id, no pending/publish import state, no three trigger routes, and **no "the
external source is unavailable" failure path** — the failure cannot occur because the dependency does
not exist.

**What the system does instead.** The admin authors every movie by hand: title, poster, the details
customers see, and the display window (`P-ADM-01`). This is the largest change of scope on the
project.

**What keeps it possible.** The movie row's fields are the same fields an import would have populated.
An importer would be a writer against the existing admin surface, not a second model.

**Also removed with it.** The whole class of failure where a scheduled job silently overwrites
something a person typed.

**Phase.** n/a — Phase 6 became admin movie management in its place.

---

### `P-SCP-07` · No scheduled job of any kind · `RULED`
`[SRC: SRC-003 OPEN-PROC-01 · SRC-002 §E E-4 · FR-ADR-005]`
`[BRD: R-OUT-07]`

**Not built.** No scheduler process, no cron container, no EventBridge rule, no periodic task inside
the API or the worker. **No later design may introduce one.**

**What the system does instead.** Everything that would otherwise have been swept by a job is either
self-expiring or done on the read path:

| What a job would have done | What happens instead |
|---|---|
| release expired seat holds | the Redis key's TTL expires on its own — no cleanup job (`SRC-002 §8.1.4`, `P-HLD-05`) |
| prune old idempotency records | nothing is ever deleted (`FR-ADR-012`) |
| drain the receipt outbox | the worker's existing consume loop relays it (`FR-ADR-031`) |
| refresh a dashboard rollup | the figures are computed on the read path (`P-RPT-02`) |
| expire a movie's display window | the window is evaluated at read time against the current instant (`P-BRW-06`) |

**The discipline this imposes**, stated because it is the point: anything that would otherwise have
been "the nightly job will fix it" has to be correct when it is written. That is stricter and it is
deliberate.

**What keeps it possible.** Three long-running processes exist, not four (`FR-ADR-005`); adding a
fourth is a task-definition change, not an application redesign. It would also cost memory the budget
does not have (`S7.12`).

**Phase.** n/a.

---

### `P-SCP-08` · No separate section for upcoming releases · `RULED`
`[SRC: SRC-003 OPEN-TMDB-02 · SRC-001 §E E-5 · FR-ADR-021]`
`[BRD: R-OUT-08]`

**Not built.** No "coming soon" listing, no pre-sale, no notify-me.

**What the system does instead.** Customers see only what is currently showing: published, and inside
its display window, evaluated against the current instant (`P-BRW-06`). A movie the admin has authored
but whose window has not opened is invisible to customers and visible to the admin.

**What keeps it possible.** The display window already has a start. A future-dated movie is already
representable — it is simply not rendered. Showing it would be a listing change, not a data change.

**Phase.** n/a.

---

### `P-SCP-09` · No scannable code on the ticket · `RULED`
`[SRC: SRC-003 OPEN-TICKET-01 · SRC-001 §E E-9 · SRC-002 §E E-5 · FR-ADR-015]`
`[BRD: R-OUT-09]`

**Not built.** No QR code, no barcode, no image generated anywhere, in the email or on screen.

**What the system does instead.** A **unique booking reference**, `FR-XXXX-XXXX`, designed to be read
aloud from a phone screen and typed by a person at a door (`P-TKT-01`). Its alphabet excludes the
characters people confuse.

**What keeps it possible.** The reference is a stable value on the booking row. Encoding it into an
image later changes the receipt template and nothing else.

**Phase.** n/a.

---

### `P-SCP-10` · No scanner, no validation endpoint, and no used-ticket state · `RULED`
`[SRC: SRC-003 OPEN-TICKET-02 · SRC-001 §E E-3 · FR-ADR-048]`
`[BRD: R-OUT-10]`

**Not built.** No scanning device, no door application, no endpoint that validates a reference, no
`used_at` column, no check-in record, and **no cinema-staff role** (`P-SCP-15`).

**What the system does instead.** Entry is a person at the entrance reading the reference from the
customer's receipt and checking it by hand.

**Accepted weakness, stated rather than buried.** **Nothing prevents the same reference being
presented twice.** That is accepted for a demonstration project and it is a real hole in a live one
(`SRC-003 OPEN-TICKET-02`).

**What keeps it possible.** The booking row is the record a validation endpoint would read and a
`used_at` column would sit on. Adding one is an additive migration.

**Phase.** n/a.

---

### `P-SCP-11` · No customer cancellation and no refund of any kind · `RULED` · reserved: money
`[SRC: SRC-003 OPEN-CANCEL-01 · SRC-003 OPEN-CANCEL-02 · SRC-001 §E E-2 · FR-ADR-013]`
`[BRD: R-OUT-11]`

**Not built.** No cancellation control, no cancellation endpoint, no refund of any kind — partial or
full, for any reason. No refund table, no refund amount, no cancellation reason, no policy
configuration. **The payment path has no reverse**: a captured simulated payment is never unwound.

**What the system does instead.** A confirmed booking is final (`P-PAY-08`).

**Recorded, not challenged.** **A customer who cannot attend loses their money.** That is the ruled
behaviour for a demonstration project and it would need revisiting before a real customer ever booked.

**What keeps it possible.** The schema carries a booking `status` and a `cancelled_at` timestamp, and
**no v1 endpoint exposes either** (`FR-ADR-013`). `status` is written once at confirmation;
`cancelled_at` stays null for every row v1 creates. Adding those columns after real bookings exist
would be a migration on live data with a backfill nobody can verify.

**One thing that must be revisited first if cancellation is ever added**: the unique constraint on
`(showtime_id, seat_id)` is **total**, not partial. With no cancellation that is the simpler and
stricter form. A cancelled booking under a total constraint would hold its seat forever.

**Phase.** n/a.

---

### `P-SCP-12` · No real payment provider, ever, at any point in this project · `RULED` · reserved: money
`[SRC: SRC-003 OPEN-PAY-01 · SRC-003 OPEN-PAY-02 · SRC-001 §E E-10 · FR-ADR-041]`
`[BRD: R-OUT-12]`

**Not built.** No gateway integration, no merchant account, no webhook receiver, no card number field,
no CVV field, no expiry field, and **no placeholder for one**. No card data in a log, a column, a test
fixture or a seed script.

**What the system does instead.** A simulated provider behind a real interface with real state
transitions — `pending → authorized → captured` and `failed` — and an artificial delay bounded well
below the three-minute hold (`P-PAY-03`). The checkout screen states plainly that no real payment is
taken, as a persistent full-width element that is never a footnote and never dismissible.

**The safety rule, and why it is the sharpest one in this document.** `PAYMENT_PROVIDER` has **no
default** (`FR-ADR-041`, `S7.9`). A default would let a deployment become a fake shop silently, and
**a simulated payment that looks real to a customer is the worst failure this product can produce** —
it takes their seat, takes nothing else, and they find out at the door.

**What keeps it possible.** The interface is shaped so a real provider drops in behind it without a
schema change. `FR-ADR-041` rules a real provider out entirely, so this is a property of the design
and not a plan.

**Phase.** n/a.

---

### `P-SCP-13` · No accessible-seat marking, no paired seats, and no gap rule · `RULED`
`[SRC: SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-02 · SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-03 · SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-04 · FR-ADR-016]`
`[BRD: R-OUT-13]`

**Not built.** No wheelchair-accessible seat flag, no seat sold only in a pair, and no rule preventing
a customer leaving a single empty seat between bookings.

**What the system does instead.** Every seat is sold individually and any available seat may be chosen
(`P-SEA-03`). **The lock stays per seat**, which keeps the hardest part of this system at its simplest
form — a paired seat would turn the lock from per-seat into per-group, which is a materially harder
concurrency problem.

**Recorded, not challenged.** A real cinema in India operates under accessibility obligations, and
this ruling rests on there being no real customers. **This would need revisiting before anyone booked
a real seat** (`SRC-003 OPEN-SEAT-02`). It is a known deferral, not an oversight.

**What keeps it possible.** A seat row already carries a category by foreign key; a flag or a grouping
would be an additive column. The gap rule is the expensive one to add later — it is a rule that can
make a valid selection fail at confirmation time, so it would have to be enforced where the map is
drawn as well as at checkout.

**Phase.** n/a.

---

### `P-SCP-14` · No export of reporting or booking data to a file · `RULED`
`[SRC: SRC-003 OPEN-REPORT-02 · FR-ADR-043]`
`[BRD: R-OUT-14]`

**Not built.** No CSV, no spreadsheet, no PDF, no download control, no print-to-file path, and no
endpoint that returns a file.

**What the system does instead.** The dashboard is on screen only (`P-RPT-05`).

**Why this is more than a missing feature.** It keeps customer-level booking data off any download
path. For a business with no operations team, a file of booking data that leaves the business's
control the moment it is created is a real exposure, and not creating it removes the exposure rather
than managing it.

**What keeps it possible.** The dashboard's figures come from one query layer; an export would
serialise the same result differently.

**Phase.** n/a.

---

### `P-SCP-15` · No cinema-staff role and no door scanner · `RULED` · rests on a `PROVISIONAL` reading
`[SRC: SRC-003 OPEN-ROLE-01 · SRC-001 §E E-1 · FR-ADR-009]`
`[BRD: R-OUT-15]`

**Not built.** There is no cinema-staff role. `SRC-001 §4.3` — a staff member checking customers in by
scanning a ticket code — is withdrawn, and `§5.5.3` with it.

**What the system does instead.** Four roles: guest, customer, manager, admin (`S3.1`). Entry is a
manual human check (`P-SCP-10`).

**⚠ The role set is `PROVISIONAL`** (`SRC-003 C-1`). The client's own answers had to be reconciled.
What is **not** provisional is the removal of the staff role — the ruling kills the door-scanner
persona explicitly, in the same sentence.

**What keeps it possible.** The role is a value on the user row and an authorisation dependency on a
router. Adding one is additive; the reason four were modelled rather than three is that **collapsing a
role later is a migration and adding one later is a rewrite of every authorisation dependency**, so
the wider set is the safer error.

**Phase.** n/a.

---

### `P-SCP-16` · No discounts, no concession pricing, no fees, and no separate tax line · `RULED` · reserved: money and legal
`[SRC: SRC-003 OPEN-PRICE-02 · SRC-003 OPEN-PRICE-03 · FR-ADR-040]`
`[BRD: R-OUT-16]`

**Not built.** No discount code field, no student or concession rate, no booking fee, no convenience
fee, no separate tax line, and **no space left on any screen for one**.

**What the system does instead.** The amount charged is the sum of the seat prices, with nothing added
and nothing taken away (`P-PAY-07`). The price shown is the price paid.

**Recorded, not challenged, and this is the irreversible part.** A real cinema in India would show GST
on a ticket. **The stored total is a single figure and cannot be split into net and tax afterwards**,
because nothing records what portion was ever meant to be tax. That is written down so it is a known
deferral rather than something an accountant discovers.

**What keeps it possible.** Going forward, a tax or fee would be a second stored component alongside
the seat total. Historical bookings would remain single figures and would have to stay that way.

**Phase.** n/a.

---

### `P-SCP-17` · No artificial-intelligence feature · `RULED` · reserved: legal
`[SRC: SRC-003 OPEN-MODEL-01]`
`[BRD: R-OUT-17]`

**Not built.** No recommendation model, no natural-language surface, no model call anywhere in the
product, and **no customer data sent to any model**.

**What the system does instead.** Listings sort by the customer's chosen filter, defaulting to newest
first (`P-BRW-05`). That is an ordering, not a recommendation.

**A distinction worth stating.** This governs **the product**. That the product is *built* by LLMs
reading this repository is a separate matter, and it is why the repository holds no credential and no
real customer data.

**What keeps it possible.** Nothing in the design forecloses it, and adding one would be a reserved
decision (`S7.17`), not a technical one.

**Phase.** n/a.

---

### `P-SCP-18` · Withdrawing a showtime that already has paid bookings — **not excluded, unruled** · **`OPEN`** · reserved: money, irreversible
`[SRC: SRC-003 OPEN-SHOWCANCEL-01 · SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-03 · SRC-003 OPEN-CANCEL-02 · FR-ADR-023]`
`[BRD: R-OUT-18]`

**This row is not an exclusion. It is an open question, and it is listed here so its absence from the
admin surface is visible rather than silent.**

`SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-03` names *"cancel a show"* as something only the admin does. `OPEN-CANCEL-02` said
to forget cinema-cancelled shows, and there are no refunds. **Those customers have paid.** What
happens to their bookings, and to their money, is a decision about money that no model may make.

**What v1 does.** **The admin has no way to withdraw a showtime.** No endpoint, no control, no screen
(`P-ADM-09`). That gap is stated to the client rather than left to be found. It is the only capability
the client named that this version does not deliver.

**Why that is the right shape while the row is open.** An unbuilt capability is recoverable. An
unrefunded customer is not.

**What may not be written here.** No withdrawal flow, no refund behaviour, no customer notification,
and no policy — not as a default, not as a placeholder, not as a suggestion in a comment. **Escalate,
never invent.**

**Phase.** blocked, pending `OPEN-SHOWCANCEL-01`.

---

## S2.5 The rule that governs the whole section

**Excluded is not blocked** (`SRC-001 §6.6`, `FR-ADR-010`, `FR-ADR-013`, `FR-ADR-046`).

> *"We may ask for these later, so please do not design in a way that blocks them."*

**An exclusion that hardens into an architectural impossibility is a defect, not a simplification**
(`CONSTITUTION.md` Art I.3). Four places where this rule is already doing visible work in the
specification rather than only in prose:

- the `cinema` entity stays in the schema with exactly one row, so a second venue is an insert and not
  a migration against live bookings (`FR-ADR-010`);
- booking `status` and `cancelled_at` exist and no endpoint exposes them (`P-SCP-11`);
- the **cinema filter capability exists and is not rendered** while one cinema exists, and appears on
  its own if a second ever does (`P-BRW-03`);
- the payment interface keeps real state transitions so a provider could drop in behind it, even
  though `P-SCP-12` rules one out entirely.

**And one place where the rule has a limit, stated because the limit is real**: `P-SCP-16` and
`P-SCP-02` both note that the stored total is a single figure. Adding a tax line or an order line
later works **going forward only**. History cannot be reinterpreted, and pretending otherwise would be
the kind of quiet promise this document exists to avoid.

---

# S3 — Personas, roles, and the surface inventory

---

## S3.1 The four roles

> ## ⚠ `PROVISIONAL` — one message from the client reverses this
> `[SRC: SRC-003 C-1 · SRC-003 OPEN-ROLE-01 · SRC-003 OPEN-SCOPE-01 · SRC-003 OPEN-REPORT-01 ·
> SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-03 · SRC-001 §E E-1 · FR-ADR-009]`
>
> This is a **build-session reading that reconciles two of the client's own answers**, not a literal
> answer. `SRC-003 C-1` records it, including the reading that was rejected. **Read `C-1` before
> relying on anything in this section.**

`SRC-001 §4` named five user types. `SRC-002 §3.1` implied one. Under `CONSTITUTION.md` Art II.2 that
is a contradiction inside the client's own instructions and the build session may not pick a
favourite, so it went back as `OPEN-ROLE-01`.

**The answer created a second contradiction inside itself.** `OPEN-ROLE-01` says *"do not make more
personas… only 1 admin persona. admin can do all the stuff the managers can do."* The very next
answer, `OPEN-SCOPE-01`, describes *"2 managers per cinema hall"* who *"can see earnings movies for
the day, month, week and cannot add the new movies"*, and `OPEN-REPORT-01` gives managers a dashboard.

**Read as four roles.** The prohibition is aimed at the cinema-staff and door-scanner persona, which
the same sentence kills explicitly, and at admin *tiers* — not at managers, whom two later answers
describe in operational detail. *"Admin can do all the stuff the managers can do"* states that admin
is a superset of manager, which presupposes that manager exists.

**The rejected reading** was three roles, with the manager dashboard served to admins filtered by
hall. It satisfies `OPEN-ROLE-01` literally, and it discards "2 managers per cinema hall" entirely and
puts twelve people on one shared admin account — which destroys the business's ability to answer who
changed what, because every audit row would name the same actor.

| Role | Account | What they can do | Modelled as |
|---|---|---|---|
| **guest** | none | browse movies, showtimes and the seat map. **Cannot hold and cannot book** | the absence of a session; not a row |
| **customer** | required | hold seats, pay, view their own bookings and receipts | `user.role = 'customer'` |
| **manager** | required | **read only** — the dashboard for the screens they are assigned to | `user.role = 'manager'` + `manager_screen_assignment` |
| **admin** | required | everything, including everything a manager can do | `user.role = 'admin'` |

**Roles are one column on the user row**, not a many-to-many table (`FR-ADR-050`). The four are
mutually exclusive; admin is a superset of manager **by capability, not by composition**, so a role
table would model a combination that cannot exist.

**Four are modelled rather than three because collapsing a role later is a migration and adding one
later is a rewrite of every authorisation dependency.** The wider set is the safer error.

**If the client reverses this to three roles**, the `manager` role value, the assignment table and the
manager router are removed and the dashboard is served to admins with a screen filter. That is a
contained change, and it is why the reading was recorded rather than buried.

## S3.2 The two personas that no longer exist

`[SRC: SRC-001 §E E-1 · SRC-003 OPEN-TICKET-02 · FR-ADR-009]`

**There is no cinema-staff role and no door scanner.** `SRC-001 §4.3` — withdrawn by erratum `E-1` —
described a staff member checking customers in by scanning a ticket code, and `§5.5.3`, withdrawn by
`E-3`, had staff validating tickets at the door. **Both are dead text and neither is live authority.**

**Entry is a person at the entrance reading the booking reference from the customer's emailed receipt
and checking it by hand** (`P-TKT-06`, `P-SCP-10`). There is no scanning device, no validation
endpoint, and nothing that marks a reference as used.

## S3.3 A manager writes nothing, and that is a rule and not a default

`[SRC: SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-03 · SRC-001 §7.4 · FR-ADR-009 · FR-ADR-011]`

The client ruled: *"the admin will only be the one who does changes in movie, cancel a show or other
priviledged things..no other persona."*

**A manager endpoint that writes anything is a defect, not a feature. There is no small, safe write.**

`OPEN-SCOPE-01`'s *"add more stuff that managers can do"* is read as **more reporting only**, because
`OPEN-OPS-03` puts every write on the admin. Anything beyond reporting is a proposal for the client to
approve, never assumed scope — and this document proposes none.

## S3.4 A manager sees their own screens and nobody else's

`[SRC: SRC-001 §4.4 · SRC-003 OPEN-SCOPE-01 · SRC-003 C-2 · FR-ADR-011]`

- Scope attaches to the **screen**, not to the cinema. That matches the ruling's own words —
  *"different managers for different cinema hall"* — and it is the **stricter** option: with one
  cinema, cinema-level scoping would scope nothing and the access-control test would pass vacuously
  while protecting nothing.
- **"Two managers per hall" is an observation of the client's current staffing, not a constraint.**
  No check constraint, no trigger and no application rule enforces the number two. The schema permits
  one, three or zero. Making it a rule would turn every legitimate staffing change into a migration.
- **A manager may be assigned to more than one screen.**
- **A manager with no assignment sees an empty dashboard. That is the correct state for a new
  account, not an error, and it must not render as one.**

**How this is tested** (`CONSTITUTION.md` Art VI.5): assign manager A to screen 1, create bookings on
screens 1 and 2, then assert A's dashboard returns a **non-empty, non-zero** figure for screen 1 and a
denied result for screen 2. **Both halves are required.** A test asserting only "denied" passes
against a query that returns nothing for anybody.

## S3.5 Authorisation is applied once, on the router

`[SRC: SRC-001 §7.4 · CONSTITUTION.md Art VI.4 · FR-ADR-009 · FR-ADR-011]`

Every endpoint in `S6` carries an `authorisation_rule`. **That rule is enforced by a dependency
attached to a router, never by a check inside a handler.** A per-handler check is the pattern that
eventually misses one, and `SRC-001 §7.4` requires that staff and management functions are not
reachable by customers.

There are four routers, and the boundary between them is the authorisation model:

| Router | Prefix | Endpoints | Dependency |
|---|---|---|---|
| public | `/api/movies`, `/api/showtimes`, `/api/reference`, `/api/auth` | 12 | none — no session required |
| customer | `/api/me`, `/api/bookings`, `/api/holds`, `/api/auth/me` | 10 | a valid session, **and the resource's owner must be the caller** |
| reporting | `/api/reports` | 3 | role `manager` or `admin`; the dependency resolves the caller's assigned screen ids and **every query filters on that set**. One route inside it, `/api/reports/audit`, narrows further to `admin` |
| admin | `/api/admin` | 30 | role `admin` only. **Every privileged write in the product is behind this one prefix** |
| operational | `/health`, `/metrics` | 3 | none, and **not routed to the public through the load balancer** |

**One route is admin-only without sitting under `/api/admin`**: `EP-RPT-04` `GET /api/reports/audit`,
the change log. It is a **read**, so it belongs to the reporting router by shape, and it narrows to
`admin` because `SRC-003 OPEN-OPS-03` gives reading the audit trail to the admin alone. Recorded here
because a reviewer checking "everything admin-only is under `/api/admin`" would otherwise read it as a
misplacement.

**The manager router resolves the screen set in the dependency, never from a screen id in the
request.** A handler that reads a screen id from the request and checks it itself is the pattern this
rule exists to prevent. An admin runs the same queries with **no** screen filter — that difference,
and not an assignment row, is what makes an admin a superset of a manager.

**A manager who reaches an admin write path receives `FORBIDDEN` (403) from the router**, before any
handler runs.

## S3.7 What each persona arrives wanting, and leaves with

| Persona | Arrives wanting | Leaves with | Fails if |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Guest** | to know what is on and whether a good seat is free | either a decision to register, or an answer | they must register before they can see whether a seat is free |
| **Customer, first visit** | a specific seat at a specific showtime | a booking reference on screen and a receipt on its way | they lose their selection at the registration step (`P-ACC-05`) |
| **Customer, returning** | the same, faster | the same, inside two minutes (`SC-1`) | the seat map lags, or the three minutes runs out unannounced |
| **Customer, at the door** | to get in | to be let in on the reference | the receipt never arrived — **`OPEN-EMAILFAIL-01`, unruled** |
| **Manager** | last night's numbers for their halls | occupancy, takings and per-film performance for **their** screens | they can see another manager's halls, or their own dashboard returns nothing and reads as an error |
| **Admin** | a film on sale by Friday | a published movie with showtimes and prices | a change they made is not attributable to them (`P-ADM-11`) |
| **Operator** *(the same person as the admin, `R-CON-02`)* | to know the product is up, and to find an incident a customer described | one alarm, a request id, and an honest list of what nobody is watching | they believe one alarm is monitoring (`S7.14`) |

## S3.9 One consequence of one person holding every role

`[SRC: SRC-003 OPEN-NAME-01 · SRC-001 §8.2 · FR-ADR-068 · CONSTITUTION.md Art IX.7]`

The client is the customer-facing business, the developer, the money-signer, the rules-signer and the
operator, **and there is no backup** — stated affirmatively, not left blank.

Two consequences that this document must not paper over:

- **There is no escalation path and there cannot be.** If the one alarm is not read, nothing else
  happens (`S7.14`).
- **The delay in which a bad decision usually becomes visible never occurs**, because the decider is
  also at the keyboard. That is why a fresh zero-context reader graded this document, and why the
  substitution is recorded in `S8.6` rather than passed off as independent review.

# S4 — Product specifications, by epic

## S4 / E1 — Browse and discover

#### `P-BRW-01` · Show a movie only when it is published and inside its display window · `RULED`
`[SRC: SRC-003 OPEN-ROLE-01 · SRC-003 OPEN-TMDB-01 · SRC-003 OPEN-TMDB-03 · SRC-003 OPEN-LOCALE-01 · FR-ADR-021 · FR-ADR-018]`
`[BRD: R-BRW-06]`

**Behaviour.** A movie appears on any customer-facing surface only when both gates pass:

1. `published_at IS NOT NULL` — the admin published it deliberately.
2. `display_from <= T < display_until` — the evaluation instant `T` falls inside the display window.

A movie failing either gate is invisible to guests and customers alike. It is never deleted and never
hidden from the admin (`FR-ADR-012`, `FR-ADR-021`).

**How the gates are evaluated, exactly.**

- `published_at`, `display_from` and `display_until` are `timestamptz` columns holding UTC instants
  (`FR-ADR-018`). There is no `timestamp without time zone` anywhere in this path.
- **`published_at` is a record of *when*, not a scheduling gate.** The read path tests only
  `IS NOT NULL`. It never compares `published_at` to the clock. A future-dated `published_at` would
  duplicate what `display_from` already means, and two columns expressing one fact drift.
- **`display_from` is inclusive, `display_until` is exclusive** (`FR-ADR-021`). The predicate is
  `display_from <= T` and `T < display_until`. A movie at exactly `display_until` is out.
- **`T` is the current instant from the injected clock** (`FR-ADR-018`), compared as an instant. No
  local date is derived to make this comparison — instant against instant, so the comparison is
  correct regardless of the server's zone.
- **The admin submits both instants and the server converts nothing.** `display_from` and
  `display_until` are stored exactly as submitted. `EP-ADM-04` accepts a local date **and time**
  (`P-ADM-04`, `SCR-ADM-02`), and **the admin types the exclusive end** — so a film whose last day is
  the 20th is given `display_until = 2026-08-21T00:00:00+05:30` by the person entering it, not by the
  server. **No day is added anywhere on the write path.**

  > **This overturns what this row said before.** It previously claimed the admin picked a last *date*
  > and the server moved it to the day after. That was wrong on two counts. `EP-ADM-04` is rank 1 and
  > accepts an instant, so the wire settles it; and **a server that silently shifts what an admin typed
  > by a day is the worse of the two designs even where it is convenient**, because the admin gets no
  > signal in either direction — they cannot tell from the form whether the 20th they typed means the
  > 20th or the 21st, and the first evidence either way is a customer finding the film gone a day
  > early. The exclusive boundary is now stated **once**, at the point of entry, where the person
  > choosing it can see it. `SCR-ADM-02`'s help text is what makes that legible and it belongs to the
  > admin lane.
- **Both columns are NULLABLE, and a null is treated as "not visible".** The window predicate is
  `display_from <= T AND T < display_until`, and **a null on either side fails it** — there is no
  three-valued subtlety to reason about, because the row is excluded exactly as a row outside its
  window is. The read path needs no special case and no `COALESCE`.
- **A draft with no window is a normal mid-authoring state, not a fault.** An admin creates a film
  before deciding when it runs (`P-ADM-01`), so the columns are null between the insert and the
  moment the dates are chosen. **Publication is where the window becomes mandatory**, not the insert:
  `P-ADM-05` refuses to publish a film whose window is missing, and `SCR-ADM-02` publishes the gate
  line `No display window set.` So a published film always has both, which is the invariant the
  client's "a dealine of how long this will stay" (`SRC-003 OPEN-ROLE-01`) actually asks for, and an
  open-ended **run** is still not a state this product has — a long run is a far `display_until`.

  > **This overturns what this row said before, and the earlier text was the defect.** It stated
  > *"Both columns are `NOT NULL`"*, which contradicts every admin row that touches them:
  > `P-ADM-01`'s draft insert names three nulls and not these, `EP-ADM-02` does not accept the window
  > at all, and `EP-ADM-03` returns both as *"ISO-8601 instant or null"*. **Under `NOT NULL` the
  > first admin write in the product is impossible** — there is no endpoint that could supply the
  > value the constraint demands — and `P-ADM-05`'s entire `PUBLISH_BLOCKED` branch plus two
  > published strings become unreachable code. **Nothing about how the gate is evaluated changes**;
  > everything above this bullet stands, and it is why this row owns the read path.

**Who may do it.** guest · customer · manager · admin — all four, identically. The gate is a query
predicate, not an authorisation rule; there is no role that sees more on the browse surface. The
router applies no auth dependency to these routes (`SRC-001 §7.4`, `FR-ADR-014`).

**Preconditions.** At least one movie row exists. The cinema row carries its IANA zone name
(`FR-ADR-018`). A clock is injected into the domain layer.

**Happy path.**
1. A request arrives at any customer-facing movie, showtime or seat-map surface.
2. The service reads `T` from the injected clock.
3. The visibility predicate — **one function, called from every such query** — is applied.
4. Rows failing either gate are absent from the result. They are not returned with a flag.

**Exception paths.**

| # | Trigger | Server | What the user sees, verbatim |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Every published movie is outside its window | 200 with an empty list | "Nothing is showing right now." |
| 2 | The filters chosen match no visible movie | 200 with an empty list | "Nothing is showing for the chosen filters." |
| 3 | A movie id that exists but fails a gate is requested directly | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | "That movie is not showing." |
| 4 | A movie id that has never existed is requested | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | "That movie is not showing." |
| 5 | PostgreSQL is unreachable | 503 `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` | "The site is temporarily unavailable. Please try again in a moment." |

Rows 3 and 4 return the **same** response on purpose. A different answer for "unpublished" and "never
existed" tells an anonymous caller which draft movie ids exist.

**Server-side validation.** `movie_id` is a positive integer; a non-integer or a value below 1 is
422 `VALIDATION_FAILED` and never reaches the query. The visibility predicate is applied in SQL, not by
filtering in Python after the fetch — a post-fetch filter is the one a later refactor drops.

**Worked example.** A movie the admin published on 2026-08-10, to be shown from 2026-08-14 to
2026-08-20 inclusive.

```
published_at   = 2026-08-10T11:04:22+05:30   (stored 2026-08-10T05:34:22Z)
display_from   = 2026-08-14T00:00:00+05:30   (stored 2026-08-13T18:30:00Z)
display_until  = 2026-08-21T00:00:00+05:30   (stored 2026-08-20T18:30:00Z)
                 ↑ the ADMIN typed the 21st, because the bound is exclusive.
                   The server stored what it was given and added no day.
```

| Evaluation instant `T` | `published_at` gate | window gate | Visible |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-13T23:59:59+05:30 | passes | `T < display_from` | **no** |
| 2026-08-14T00:00:00+05:30 | passes | `display_from <= T`, inclusive | **yes** |
| 2026-08-20T23:59:59+05:30 | passes | still `T < display_until` | **yes** |
| 2026-08-21T00:00:00+05:30 | passes | `T = display_until`, exclusive | **no** |

The same movie with `published_at = NULL` is invisible at every one of those four instants.

#### `P-BRW-02` · Carry the six details a customer chooses between films on · `RULED`
`[SRC: SRC-001 §5.1.1 · SRC-003 OPEN-TMDB-01 · FR-ADR-021 · FR-ADR-061]`
`[BRD: R-BRW-02]`

**Behaviour.** Every movie in the listing carries its poster, synopsis, running time, certification,
language and genre. `SRC-001 §5.1.1` survives unchanged and names exactly those six.

**The listing payload per movie.**

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | internal id; public because a movie is not private (`FR-ADR-017`) |
| `title` | string | not unique — two films may share a title, and a re-release is a second row (`FR-ADR-021`) |
| `synopsis` | string | plain text, no markup |
| `runtime_minutes` | integer | rendered as a number, in `--fr-font-mono` |
| `certification` | `{id, name}` | a lookup row, not free text. **`name`, not `code`** — see below |
| `language` | `{id, name}` | a lookup row, because it is a filter facet |
| `genres` | array of `{id, name}` | many-to-many; a film is routinely two genres |
| `poster_url` | string | the **path to this API's poster redirect**, never an S3 URL and never a third party's URL |
| `display_until` | string | ISO-8601 with the `+05:30` offset. The **exclusive** end of this film's display window (`P-BRW-01`). **Never null on this surface** — the column is nullable, but a film that reaches a customer-facing listing has passed the window gate, which a null fails. Carried on the listing because the date strip is built from it (`P-BRW-04`) |

**The certification is `{id, name}` and there is no `code` anywhere.** This wire shape previously read
`{id, code}` in five places and **nothing could ever have populated it**: `P-ADM-23` owns the
`certification` table and fixes it at `id`, `name`, `is_active`, `created_at`, saying in terms that
there is no code, and `EP-ADM-26` accepts only `name`. **The data model is right and the wire was
wrong**, so the wire changed. **No `code` column is added** — adding a column because a display field
asked for one is a data-model change made from the wrong end, and the table is `P-ADM-23`'s.

`name` already holds exactly the text the certification chip renders, because it is the only thing the
admin types. The change also makes `certification` the same shape as `language`, `genre` and `format`:
four vocabularies of one table shape had no business carrying two wire shapes.

**Who may do it.** guest · customer · manager · admin. Public.

**Preconditions.** The movie passes both gates in `P-BRW-01`. A published movie always has a poster
(`FR-ADR-021` makes it a publish-time check), so `poster_url` is never null on this surface.

**Happy path.**
1. The listing query returns the visible movies with their lookup rows joined.
2. `poster_url` is built as `/api/movies/{id}/poster` from configuration, not stored.
3. The card renders the poster box at its reserved aspect ratio before the image arrives.

**Exception paths.**

| # | Trigger | Server | What the user sees, verbatim |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The poster object is missing from S3 or the image fails to load in the browser | the redirect returns 404 `NOT_FOUND`; the listing is unaffected | the poster box draws the perforation motif with the title inside it; no words are added |
| 2 | A movie row has no genre | 200; `genres` is an empty array | the metadata row omits the genre segment; nothing says "unknown" |
| 3 | The synopsis is longer than three lines | 200; the full text is sent | the card clamps to three lines; the detail screen shows all of it |

**Server-side validation.** None on this path — it is a read with no client-supplied field. The
constraint that matters is upstream: a movie cannot be published with a null poster (`FR-ADR-021`).

**Worked example.** Not applicable. This spec computes no number.

**`OPEN-ATTRIB-01` bites here.** No licensed image, title or synopsis enters this product while that
row is open. Demonstration content is `DEMO MOVIE 01` with no image from anywhere (`FR-ADR-067`).
