## S5 / E2 — Seat selection and the hold

#### `SCR-SEA-01` · The seat map and the price summary
**Route.** `/showtimes/{showtime_id}` · **Who reaches it.** guest, customer, manager, admin —
everyone; the map is public · **Component basis.** `COMPONENTS.md §1` (the seat map), `§2` (the
legend), `§5` (the price summary)

> **One screen, two halves. `SCR-SEA-01` and lane E1's `SCR-BRW-03` are the same screen at the same
> route, `/showtimes/{showtime_id}` — not two destinations and not two routes.** `SCR-BRW-03`
> specifies the **read path** on this screen: the layout that arrives, how it is drawn, how it
> refreshes and how stale it may be. This section specifies the **interactive layer on that same
> screen**: what a tap does, the price summary, the countdown, the hold and every way it fails.
> **There is no `/seats` route.** Where the two sections name the same element, the copy is the same
> string, converged deliberately — the sold-out banner and the poll-failure strip in particular; a
> variant found in either file is a defect, not a choice.

**What the user arrives with / leaves with.** They arrive with a showtime id and, if they came back
from signing in, a restored selection in `sessionStorage`. They leave with either a live hold — a hold
token, an `expires_at` and a total, all in `sessionStorage` — or nothing at all.

**Fields and controls.**

| Element | Token(s) | Behaviour | Validation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Map field | `--fr-surface-inset`, padding `--fr-space-4` | scrolls horizontally inside its own container; the page body never scrolls sideways | none |
| Screen bar and falloff | `--fr-screen-bar`, `--fr-radius-pill`, gradient from `--fr-screen-glow` | fixed at the top of the field; carries no state | none |
| `SCREEN` label | `--fr-ink-muted`, `--fr-text-xs`, `--fr-track-caps` | centred inside the falloff, below the bar | none |
| Row gutter | width `--fr-seat-gutter`, `--fr-font-mono`, `--fr-text-xs`, `--fr-ink-muted` | pinned left while the map scrolls | none |
| Seat cell, `available` | fill `--fr-seat-available`, 1px `--fr-seat-edge-available`, number in `--fr-seat-ink`, `--fr-seat-size` square, `--fr-radius-sm` | tappable; a tap adds it to the selection | client-side only; the hold endpoint is the enforcement point |
| Seat cell, `held_by_me` | fill `--fr-seat-mine`, 2px `--fr-seat-edge-mine`, tick in `--fr-seat-ink-mine` | tappable; a tap gives the seat back if it is held, or removes it from the selection if it is only chosen | `P-HLD-08` |
| Seat cell, `held_by_other` | fill `--fr-seat-held-other`, a solid horizontal bar in `--fr-seat-ink` | not tappable | none |
| Seat cell, `sold` | fill `--fr-seat-sold`, 45° hatching in `--fr-seat-ink` | not tappable | none |
| Seat cell, `is_active: false` | **no fill** — the field's `--fr-surface-inset` shows through — 1px **dashed** `--fr-rule`, number in `--fr-ink-muted` | **not tappable in any state, for any reader.** Drawn from this row rather than from its `state`, which stays truthful on the wire | `P-SEA-01` exceptions 4 and 5; the same treatment `SCR-BRW-03` publishes |
| Band gap and band rule | `--fr-seat-band-gap`, 1px dashed `--fr-rule` | separates category bands; category is never a colour. **Drawn only between two adjacent bands**, per `P-BRW-16`, which owns the derivation | none |
| Legend | container `--fr-surface-raised`, `--fr-radius-md`, padding `--fr-space-3`, labels `--fr-text-sm` `--fr-ink`, prices `--fr-font-mono` `--fr-ink-strong`, divider `--fr-rule-quiet` | always visible, never collapsed; each swatch is the real cell at the real size | none |
| Price summary panel | `--fr-surface-raised`, `--fr-radius-lg`, `--fr-shadow-card`, padding `--fr-space-4` | under the map on a phone, beside it above 40rem | none |
| Chosen / held heading | `--fr-screen-ink`, `--fr-text-sm`, `--fr-weight-medium` | reads `3 seats chosen` before a hold and `3 seats held by you` after one. **While a hold is live and further seats are chosen, the heading keeps naming the held count and a second subheading names the chosen count**, so the two groups are never summed into one number that is true of neither. **Every number here is an interpolated count and each has a singular and a plural form published below** | none |
| Seat line | `--fr-font-mono`, `--fr-text-sm`, `--fr-ink`; category note `--fr-text-xs` `--fr-ink-muted` | one line per selected seat, with its own price | none |
| Perforation | dashed 1px `--fr-rule`, `--fr-space-3` clear above and below | marks the tear between what you chose and what you owe | none |
| Total | label `--fr-text-sm` `--fr-ink-muted` `--fr-track-caps`; figure `--fr-font-mono` `--fr-text-xl` `--fr-weight-bold` `--fr-ink-strong` | `P-SEA-04`; absent entirely when any price is unknown | none |
| Seat cap note | `--fr-text-xs`, `--fr-ink-muted` | reads `Up to 10 seats.` | `P-HLD-04` |
| Primary action | fill `--fr-surface-accent`, `--fr-ink-on-accent`, `--fr-radius-md`, min height `--fr-tap-min`, `--fr-weight-bold` | copy depends on the reader, below. **Once a hold is live with nothing further chosen it is a navigation control, not a pay control**: it routes to `/showtimes/{showtime_id}/checkout` and issues no request. **With a hold live and further seats chosen it becomes a request control again** — `Hold n more seat(s)`, re-sending `EP-HLD-01` for the new seats only | `P-HLD-01`, `P-HLD-05` |
| Secondary action | transparent, 1px `--fr-control-edge`, `--fr-accent-ink` | reads `Give up these seats`; present only while a hold is live | `P-HLD-08` |

**There is no tax line, no discount field and no booking fee, and no space is left for one.** There is
no manual refresh control.

**Both seat-count headings are published in a singular and a plural, and one of them ships.** The
number in `3 seats chosen` and `3 seats held by you` is a **count**, interpolated at render time —
never a literal — and a selection of one seat is not an edge case but the ordinary way most bookings
begin: a customer taps one seat before they tap a second. An implementer who finds only the plural
writes `{n} seats chosen` and ships `1 seats chosen` on the first tap of nearly every session. **This
is the same failure `S7.20` rule 4 spends a paragraph on for durations**, one field over, and the same
remedy: publish both forms so neither is inferred. The counts in `P-HLD-14` rows 7 and 8 —
`You are holding 6 and chose 5 more.` — are interpolated on the same terms; those two sentences carry
no noun that inflects, so they need no second form.

**The sales-closed banner names no time, and the `409` body does — deliberately, and they are
different surfaces.** This screen and lane E1's `SCR-BRW-03` are the same screen at the same route and
both assert their shared strings are byte-identical, so a banner that differed between them was a
defect by their own rule. `P-BRW-07` exception 1 publishes `Sales for this showtime have closed.`, it
is rank 2 and both screens are rank 3, so **that string ships and this screen's former time-naming
variant is gone.** What is **not** touched is `P-HLD-14` row 9's longer body,
`Sales for this showtime closed at 7:45 pm. Choose another showtime.` — that is the `409`
`SALES_CLOSED` answer to a hold *attempt*, a different surface with a different job: it explains a
refusal that just happened and tells the customer what to do next, and naming the instant is the
useful part of it. **A banner states a standing condition the customer can see for themselves; an
error explains a refused action.** The difference is intended and is written down so the next reader
does not converge them.

**Seats may be added to a live hold, and this screen is where that happens.** `P-HLD-01` step 4
acquires further seats under the **existing** token, and `P-HLD-11` spends a worked example on the
money consequence — a hold legitimately carrying two base prices, `J1 ₹333.33`, `J2 ₹333.33`,
`J3 ₹399.99`. **Until now this screen published no state in which a customer could choose a further
seat while holding one**, so that path could not be reached from the product and `P-HLD-11`'s example
could never occur. The state and its labels are published above. Two tie-breaks apply and are stated
here because the ranking does not reach them on its own: **behaviour outranks rendering on whether a
capability exists** (`S1.2.1` case 4), so a P-row describing the act settles that the act exists; and
**the screen owns a string no P-row publishes** (case 3), so these labels are this section's.

**What the total shows while further seats are chosen, and the one thing it must not claim.** The
`TOTAL` figure is the sum of the **held** seats' snapshotted prices plus the **chosen** seats' prices
as the map currently carries them. The chosen portion is **indicative until the extend succeeds**: it
is priced at whatever base is current when the extend request runs, not at the base that produced the
held prices, which is exactly what `P-HLD-11`'s two-base-price example describes. **Only the held
portion is price-protected**, because price protection is a property of a hold and those seats are not
held yet. The seat lines carry their own prices in both groups, so the figure the customer reads always
adds up from what is on screen — the property `P-SEA-04` requires — and `Continue to payment` is
reachable only when nothing further is chosen, so **the total on the checkout screen is never a total
that included an unheld seat.**

**This screen has no pay action, and the post-hold primary action is not one.** It reads
`Continue to payment` and it navigates to `SCR-PAY-01` at `/showtimes/{showtime_id}/checkout`; it
sends no request, captures nothing and cannot fail. **`SCR-PAY-01` is the only screen in the product
that carries a control which submits a payment**, and that screen says the same thing from its own
side. An earlier draft labelled this control `Pay ₹1,562.49`, which read as a pay action on a screen
that has none — the amount is already on the line directly above it, as `TOTAL` `₹1,562.49`, so
nothing is lost by removing it from the button and one screen stops claiming a capability it does not
have.

**States.**

| State | What renders |
|---|---|
| **Empty** (no seats chosen) | The map at full size. The summary panel stays at full height with the total at `₹0.00` and the note `Up to 10 seats.` A panel that appears and disappears makes the page jump under a thumb. |
| **Loading** | The field, the screen bar and the row gutters draw immediately at full size, with seat cells as `--fr-surface-inset` blocks at 60% opacity. The frame never resizes when the data lands. No spinner: the layout is the answer. Prices render as `--fr-surface-inset` blocks and the primary action is disabled. |
| **Error, first load** | The map is replaced by `The seat map could not be loaded.` in `--fr-ink` on `--fr-surface-inset`, with a control reading `Try again`. No partial grid. |
| **Error, a poll fails** | The last good map stays on screen. A one-line strip appears at the top of the field in `--fr-ink-muted` on `--fr-surface-inset` reading `The seat map is not updating. The seats shown may be out of date.` Polling keeps retrying. |
| **Success** (a hold is granted) | Every held cell repaints to `held_by_me`, the heading changes to `3 seats held by you`, the countdown (`SCR-SEA-02`) appears, the secondary action appears, and the primary action becomes `Continue to payment`. Pressing it navigates to `/showtimes/{showtime_id}/checkout` and sends no request of its own. |
| **Hold live, further seats chosen** | A hold is live **and** the customer has tapped one or more additional `available` seats. The held cells stay `held_by_me`; the newly chosen cells render `held_by_me` too (`P-SEA-02` — there is no fifth rendering) and are listed under their own subheading in the summary. The countdown keeps running from the **unchanged** `expires_at` and does not restart. **The primary action changes from `Continue to payment` to `Hold 2 more seats`**; pressing it re-sends `EP-HLD-01` naming only the new seats, which join the existing hold under its existing token (`P-HLD-01` step 4). On success the newly chosen seats become held, the subheading disappears, and the primary action returns to `Continue to payment`. On `409 SEAT_UNAVAILABLE` the existing hold is untouched — the request is all-or-nothing over **the seats it names**, not over the whole hold (`P-HLD-07`). |
| **Partial** | The map and the price summary load independently. The map is usable before the prices arrive; the total is not rendered at all and the primary action stays disabled until every selected seat has a price. |
| **Sold out** | The full map renders, every cell `sold`, plus a banner reading `Every seat for this showtime is sold.` Not an empty state — the customer wants to see that it is genuinely full. |
| **Sales closed** | The full map renders with every cell unselectable, plus a banner. For a customer with no hold it reads `Sales for this showtime have closed.` For a customer holding seats it reads `Sales for this showtime have closed. You can still pay for the seats you are holding.` |
| **Hold expired** | Each `held_by_me` cell reverts to whatever the next poll reports — usually `available`, sometimes `held_by_other` or `sold`. Each reverting cell fires the changed-seat outline, so the customer watches the seats leave. The cells are **not** pre-emptively repainted at `0:00`; `SCR-SEA-02` is what says the hold ended. |
| **A seat changes between two polls** | The cell keeps a 2px `--fr-focus-ring` outline for `--fr-motion-change`; the fill transitions over `--fr-motion-base` with `--fr-ease-out`. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the outline is static rather than pulsing and is held for the same duration. If the seat that changed was one of the customer's own, `SCR-SEA-03` fires and names it. |

**Copy.**

| Where | Verbatim |
|---|---|
| Primary action, guest | `Sign in to hold these seats` |
| Primary action, customer, nothing chosen (disabled) | `Choose seats` |
| Primary action, customer, seats chosen | `Hold these seats` |
| Primary action, customer, hold live, **nothing further chosen** | `Continue to payment` |
| Primary action, customer, hold live, **two or more further seats chosen** | `Hold 2 more seats` — `2` renders the count of newly chosen seats, never the size of the hold |
| Primary action, customer, hold live, **exactly one further seat chosen** | `Hold 1 more seat` |
| Summary subheading, **two or more further seats chosen** | `2 more chosen` |
| Summary subheading, **exactly one further seat chosen** | `1 more chosen` |
| Secondary action, hold live | `Give up these seats` |
| Heading, before a hold, **two or more** seats | `3 seats chosen` — `3` renders the count |
| Heading, before a hold, **exactly one** seat | `1 seat chosen` |
| Heading, after a hold, **two or more** seats | `3 seats held by you` — `3` renders the count |
| Heading, after a hold, **exactly one** seat | `1 seat held by you` |
| Seat cap note | `Up to 10 seats.` — the number renders `MAX_SEATS_PER_BOOKING`; a literal `10` is a defect (`P-HLD-04`) |
| Total label | `TOTAL` |
| Empty total | `₹0.00` |
| Sold-out banner | `Every seat for this showtime is sold.` |
| Sales-closed banner, no hold | `Sales for this showtime have closed.` — `P-BRW-07` exception 1 publishes this string and this screen renders it; see the note below |
| Sales-closed banner, holding seats | `Sales for this showtime have closed. You can still pay for the seats you are holding.` |
| Map first-load failure | `The seat map could not be loaded.` |
| Map first-load retry control | `Try again` |
| Poll-failure strip | `The seat map is not updating. The seats shown may be out of date.` |
| A chosen seat has gone, on a local refresh with no sign-in involved | `C12 is no longer available. It has been removed from your choices.` — `P-SEA-03` owns it |
| A chosen seat has gone while the customer was signing in or registering | **Rendered from `P-ACC-13` (lane E5). Not restated here** |
| Legend, every label | **Rendered from `SCR-BRW-03` (lane E1), which publishes all five swatch labels and the category-row form. Not restated here** — `SCR-BRW-03` and this section are the same screen at the same route, and the legend belongs to its read-path half |
| A held seat is submitted while out of service | `Seat C12 is out of service. No seats were held.` — the set this belongs to is `P-HLD-14`'s, row 20 |

**Accessibility.** The map is **one tab stop, not 220**; arrow keys move within the grid and Enter or
Space selects. A grid of 220 tab stops is a keyboard trap with extra steps, not keyboard support. Each
seat carries an accessible name stating identity, category and state — `Row C seat 12, Premium,
available`, and `Row C seat 12, Premium, held by you` for `held_by_me`, where the number stays in the
name even though the tick has replaced it visually. An out-of-service seat reads `Row C seat 12,
Premium, out of service`, keeps its place in the arrow-key grid so the geometry does not shift under a
reader who has learned it, and never activates on Enter or Space. Every state is told apart by fill
lightness, by a mark and by a border; **colour is never the carrier**, and the out-of-service cue is
the dashed border rather than a fifth glyph, because the four glyph slots — none, bar, hatch, tick —
are already spent. Focus order is map, then legend, then summary
heading, then seat lines, then total, then primary action, then secondary action. Focus is drawn with
`--fr-focus-ring`. Seat cells are `--fr-seat-size` square, which is 24px and the WCAG 2.2 target-size
minimum; the seat is never shrunk to avoid the horizontal scroll. The primary and secondary actions are
at least `--fr-tap-min` tall. Seat-state changes announce through a live region only when they affect
the customer's own seats; a 220-seat map announcing every poll would be unusable.

#### `SCR-SEA-02` · The hold countdown
**Route.** rendered inside `/showtimes/{showtime_id}` — the one seat-map screen — and **repeated,
unchanged, on lane E3's checkout screen** · **Who reaches it.** the hold's owner only ·
**Component basis.** `COMPONENTS.md §7`

> **This specification is the single source for this component's label and its states.** The same
> component is rendered on the checkout screen; that is a repetition of this component, not a second
> one, and lane E3 specifies no label, no state and no wording for it. Any copy for the countdown that
> differs from the table below — a different label, a different zero state — is a defect in the other
> document, resolved by taking this one.

**What the user arrives with / leaves with.** It arrives with one input: the hold's `expires_at`, plus
the current instant supplied to it. It never reads the wall clock itself. It leaves the customer either
paying or back on the map.

**Fields and controls.**

| Element | Token(s) | Behaviour | Validation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Digits | `--fr-font-mono`, `--fr-text-xl`, `--fr-weight-bold`, `--fr-countdown-fill`, `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` | `m:ss`, counted down from `expires_at` | never negative; the zero state renders instead |
| Label | `--fr-text-xs`, `--fr-ink-muted`, uppercase, `--fr-track-caps` | reads `TIME LEFT` | none |
| Track | `--fr-surface-inset`, 4px tall, `--fr-radius-pill` | the full duration | none |
| Bar | `--fr-countdown-fill`, shrinking left to right | **the primary carrier** — it works with colour removed | none |
| Bar and digits, last 60 seconds | `--fr-countdown-urgent` | one threshold only, never 60/30/10 | none |
| Warning line | `--fr-text-sm`, `--fr-ink` | appears at the threshold, announced once | none |

**States.**

| State | What renders |
|---|---|
| **Empty** (no hold) | The component is absent entirely, not collapsed to zero height. |
| **Loading** | Cannot occur. The component only exists once a hold response has arrived carrying `expires_at`. |
| **Live** | Digits, bar and label. |
| **Last 60 seconds** | As live, plus the warning line, plus the two colour changes, announced once. |
| **Zero, no confirm in flight** | The countdown stops at `0:00`, the payment action is disabled, and the component states that the hold ended. It does **not** claim the seats are free, and it does **not** name a cause: reaching `0:00` is also what a graceful-shutdown release (`P-HLD-12`) and a key re-acquired by someone else (`P-HLD-03`) look like from inside the browser, and the client cannot tell the three apart. "Your three minutes are up" would therefore be a false statement in two of the three cases, which is why the copy below says only that the hold ended. |
| **Zero, a confirm in flight** | The busy state is kept and the request is not cancelled, because a request already sent cannot be un-sent. The component states that the hold has ended and that an answer is still coming. It names no cause, exactly as the other zero state does not. |
| **Error** | The component itself carries no error. `SCR-SEA-03` carries every message. |
| **Partial** | Not applicable — a hold either exists with an `expires_at` or does not. |
| **Clock skew** | If `expires_at` is already past on arrival, the zero state renders immediately. No negative numbers, ever. |

**Copy.**

| Where | Verbatim |
|---|---|
| Label | `TIME LEFT` |
| Warning at 60 seconds | `Less than a minute left. At 0:00 your seats are released and you will need to choose them again.` |
| Zero, no confirm in flight | `Your hold has ended and your seats have been released. You have not been charged.` |
| Zero, a confirm in flight | `Your hold has ended. We are waiting for the answer to your payment. Do not close this page.` |

> **⚠ Both zero states name no cause, and that is now true of the in-flight one as well.** An earlier
> draft of this box claimed the in-flight zero state still read *"Your three minutes are up"*. **It does
> not, and had not since the copy above was generalised** — the box was left behind by that edit and is
> corrected here. The copy table is the authority: the in-flight state reads `Your hold has ended. We
> are waiting for the answer to your payment. Do not close this page.`, which names the fact and not the
> reason, for the same argument that removed the clause from the other zero state — a shutdown drain
> (`P-HLD-12`) and a key re-acquired by someone else (`P-HLD-03`) reach `0:00` identically and the
> client cannot tell the three apart. **The three places that carry this string — this copy table,
> `P-HLD-09` exception path 3, and the `held_by_me_paying` + `HOLD_TTL_EXPIRE` transition in the seat
> lifecycle state machine — are byte-for-byte identical today and change together if they change at
> all.** There is no open wording item on this component.

**Accessibility.** The digits are **not** a live region — a value announced every second is unusable.
Only two events announce: the 60-second threshold, once, and the zero state, once. The bar carries the
same information as the colour, so the urgent state is legible with colour removed. The component is
not focusable and is not a control.

#### `SCR-SEA-03` · The seat-lost and hold-failure banner
**Route.** rendered inside `/showtimes/{showtime_id}`, in the scroll container's sticky header
area · **Who reaches it.** anyone who hits a failure on this lane · **Component basis.**
`COMPONENTS.md §6`

**What the user arrives with / leaves with.** It arrives with one error envelope. It leaves the
customer knowing exactly which seats went and what to press next.

**Fields and controls.**

| Element | Token(s) | Behaviour | Validation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Container | `--fr-surface-danger`, `--fr-radius-md`, padding `--fr-space-3`, 1px `--fr-control-edge` | slides in over `--fr-motion-base` with `--fr-ease-out`; sits directly above the map, visible without scrolling | none |
| Leading rule | 3px `--fr-danger-ink` down the leading edge | none | none |
| Message | `--fr-ink-on-danger`, `--fr-text-sm`, `--fr-leading-body` | the verbatim string for the `code` | none |
| Seat names inside the message | `--fr-font-mono`, `--fr-weight-bold` | taken from `details.unavailable_seats` | none |
| Action inside the banner | `--fr-accent-ink`, underlined | present only where there is something to press | none |
| Request id line | `--fr-text-xs`, `--fr-ink-muted`, `--fr-font-mono` | **5xx only** | none |

**States.**

| State | What renders |
|---|---|
| **Empty** | Nothing. The banner is absent, not collapsed to zero height. |
| **Loading** | Not applicable — a banner is the answer to a request that has already returned. |
| **Error** | One banner, carrying the message for the `code`. |
| **Success** | Not applicable — the banner never reports success. |
| **Partial** | Not applicable. |
| **Several errors at once** | **One banner.** The newest message replaces the previous one; errors never stack into a wall. |
| **Dismiss** | Only errors with nothing left to do are dismissible. `SEAT_UNAVAILABLE` is not; it clears when the customer changes the selection. |

**Copy.** The message text for every code is `P-HLD-14`'s table and this screen restates none of it.
**The banner's own two controls are this screen's to publish, and it publishes them here** — a screen
that names a control owes that control's words, and this screen named both and published neither
until now:

| Where | Verbatim |
|---|---|
| The in-banner action, on `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` — the only code that carries one | `Try again` |
| The in-banner action, accessible name | `Try again — reload the seat map` |
| The dismiss control, on a dismissible banner | `Dismiss` |
| The dismiss control, accessible name | `Dismiss this message` |

**`SCR-XCT-01` publishes a `Choose seats again` action against `HOLD_EXPIRED`; on this surface there
is none, and this row is the one that governs.** Both are rank 3, so `S1.2` alone does not separate
them — the rule that does is that **the screen owning a surface beats the cross-cutting registry for
that surface**, and the seat map is this section's. The reason is concrete rather than jurisdictional:
**a customer meeting `HOLD_EXPIRED` on the seat map is already on the screen that button would send
them to.** The control navigates nowhere. What actually happens here is automatic — the previous
selection re-applies and the map refreshes — so a button would be offering to do a thing that has
already been done, and pressing it would be indistinguishable from pressing nothing.
`SCR-XCT-01`'s action stands for every surface that is **not** the seat map and **not** `SCR-PAY-01`,
and defers to each of them by name; `SCR-PAY-01` settles the same fork on its own side for the same
reason.

**Exactly one code carries an in-banner action, and the rest carry none on purpose.**
`DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` is the only failure on this lane whose remedy is *repeating the same request*
— Redis returns and the identical action succeeds — so it is the only one where a control inside the
banner does something the customer could not do more directly. `Try again` is the string this screen
family already publishes for the map's first-load failure, reused rather than reworded, because two
words for one act is how the next variant starts. For every other code the next step is on the map
itself: `SEAT_UNAVAILABLE` wants a different seat chosen, `SEAT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` wants one deselected,
`HOLD_EXPIRED` and `HOLD_NOT_OWNED` re-apply the selection automatically, and `SALES_CLOSED` has no
next step at all. A banner button that only scrolls the customer back to where they already are is a
control with nothing to do, which is what the "present only where there is something to press" rule in
the table above exists to prevent.

**Dismissible means: nothing left to do.** `INTERNAL_ERROR` and `NOT_FOUND` are dismissible —
the customer has read them and no action follows. `SEAT_UNAVAILABLE` is not, and clears itself when
the selection changes. `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` is not, because it carries an action.

**The behaviour per code:**

| Code | What the banner does |
|---|---|
| `SEAT_UNAVAILABLE` | Names the lost seats from `details.unavailable_seats`, marks them unavailable on the map immediately, and keeps the rest of the selection |
| `HOLD_EXPIRED`, `HOLD_NOT_OWNED` | Returns the customer to the map with the previous selection re-applied and the map refreshed. **No action and not dismissible** — the return is automatic and the customer is already on the destination screen |
| `SEAT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | States the cap of ten and how many are currently held and chosen |
| `SALES_CLOSED` | Disables the map and states that sales for this showtime have closed |
| `VALIDATION_FAILED` | Names the specific problem with the selection |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | States that too many attempts were made and gives the wait, computed from `Retry-After` and rendered by **S7.20**. The banner renders the string `P-HLD-14` row 16 publishes; it formats nothing itself |
| `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` | States that seat holds are unavailable and that browsing still works. It never silently degrades. **Carries the `Try again` action; not dismissible** |
| `NOT_FOUND` | States that the showtime could not be found. **No action; dismissible** |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | The message plus the request id line. **No action; dismissible** |

**Accessibility.** The banner is announced through a live region — **an error that is only red has not
been reported.** It receives focus when it carries an action. The seat names inside the message are
plain text in `--fr-font-mono`, not links. The request id is selectable text so it can be copied.

## S5 / E3 — Checkout, money and payment

#### `SCR-PAY-01` · The checkout screen
**Route.** `/showtimes/{showtime_id}/checkout` · **Who reaches it.** An authenticated `customer`,
`manager` or `admin` holding live seats on that showtime. A `guest` cannot reach it, because a guest
cannot hold (`FR-ADR-014`, `FR-ADR-046`) · **Component basis.** `COMPONENTS.md §8` and `§8.1`, with
`§5` for the booking lines, `§6` for the error banner, `§7` for the countdown, `§0.2` for focus and
`§0.4` for money

**What the user arrives with / leaves with.** They arrive with a hold token in `sessionStorage`
(`FR-ADR-047`), an absolute `expires_at`, a seat list and a per-seat price snapshot. They leave with a
committed booking and its reference, or with a live hold and an error banner, or with an expired hold
and a return to the seat map.

**This is the only screen in the product with a pay action, and the seat map agrees.** The control the
customer presses on `SCR-SEA-01` once a hold is live reads `Continue to payment` and is **navigation
to this route** — it issues no request, captures nothing and cannot fail. The control below, labelled
`Pay ₹1,661.46`, is the only control anywhere in the product that submits `EP-PAY-01`. Both screens
state this from their own side deliberately: the claim is only checkable if the screen being excluded
also carries it.

**Fields and controls.**

| Element | Token(s) | Behaviour | Validation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Simulated-payment notice slab | `--fr-surface-notice`, `--fr-ink-on-notice`, `--fr-text-md`, `--fr-weight-medium`, `--fr-radius-md`, `--fr-space-4` | Full width, at the top of the panel, **above the heading, before anything else is read.** Persistent, never a tooltip, never dismissible, **never smaller than `--fr-text-md`.** The same colour in both themes, so a reader who has learned the dark theme still finds it unfamiliar | Not a field. It is unconditional: `PAYMENT_PROVIDER` accepts only `simulated` and any other value crashes the process at boot, so there is no runtime branch and no fetch that could fail and hide it |
| Panel | `--fr-surface-raised`, `--fr-radius-lg`, `--fr-shadow-sheet`, `--fr-space-5` | Holds everything below the notice | — |
| Heading | `--fr-font-display`, `--fr-text-xl`, `--fr-weight-black`, `--fr-track-tight`, `--fr-ink-strong` | "Confirm your booking" | — |
| Showtime line | `--fr-font-mono`, `--fr-text-sm`, `--fr-ink` | Movie title, hall and start time. **The instant arrives already carrying the cinema's UTC offset and the client renders its wall-clock part as given — it converts nothing and reads no browser timezone** (`P-PAY-01`, `P-BRW-06`, `FR-ADR-018`). The format is `S7.19`'s | — |
| Booking lines, one per seat | `--fr-font-mono`, `--fr-text-sm`, `--fr-ink`; category note `--fr-text-xs`, `--fr-ink-muted` | Seat label, category name, price. Rendered from the hold's price snapshot, never recomputed on the client from a base price | The client renders the integers it was given; it performs no arithmetic except the sum in the next row |
| Perforation above the total | dashed `--fr-stroke-hair` `--fr-rule`, `--fr-space-3` clear above and below | Marks the tear between what you chose and what you owe | — |
| Total | label `--fr-text-sm` `--fr-ink-muted` uppercase `--fr-track-caps`; figure `--fr-font-mono`, `--fr-text-xl`, `--fr-weight-bold`, `--fr-ink-strong` | The sum of the already-rounded per-seat prices (`P-PAY-04`), formatted with Indian digit grouping at render time only | If any seat price is missing the total is not shown at all and the pay action is disabled — a partial total is a wrong number |
| Countdown | `COMPONENTS.md §7`: `--fr-font-mono`, `--fr-text-xl`, `--fr-countdown-fill`; `--fr-countdown-urgent` in the last 60 seconds; track `--fr-surface-inset`, `--fr-radius-pill` | **Repeated here, not only on the seat map.** `m:ss`, computed from the server's absolute `expires_at`, never from a duration counted on the client | At `0:00` the pay action is disabled. The component never reads the wall clock; the current instant is an input |
| Pay action | `--fr-surface-accent`, `--fr-ink-on-accent`, `--fr-radius-md`, min height `--fr-tap-min`, `--fr-weight-bold` | Label is `Pay ₹1,661.46` — the figure, not a generic word. One `POST` per press; the button is disabled for the duration of the request | Disabled when: no live hold, countdown at zero, a request already in flight, or any seat price missing |
| Back to seats | transparent fill, `--fr-stroke-hair` `--fr-control-edge`, `--fr-accent-ink` | Returns to the seat map. **It does not release the hold** — there is no client-side release (`FR-ADR-047`) | — |
| Error banner | `COMPONENTS.md §6`: `--fr-surface-danger`, `--fr-ink-on-danger`, leading rule `--fr-danger-ink`, `--fr-control-edge` | Above the panel. Branches on the error `code`, never on the message text | One banner at a time; the newest replaces the previous |

**There is no card number field, no CVV field, no expiry field, no cardholder-name field and no
placeholder for any of them** (`P-PAY-08`). **There is no tax line, no discount field and no booking
fee, and no space is reserved for one** (`P-PAY-06`).

**How this screen tells "already confirmed" from "hold expired", which are entered from the same
client-visible fact.** In both, the hold token in `sessionStorage` no longer resolves to a live hold.
The screen decides from **one stored value and no request**:

| | |
|---|---|
| **What is stored** | `fr.last_booking_reference` in `sessionStorage`: the `booking_reference` from a `201` response, and the `showtime_id` it belongs to. Nothing else — no seat list, no total, no idempotency key |
| **When it is written** | On a successful confirm, from `EP-PAY-01`'s `201` body, **before** the navigation to the confirmation screen, so a customer who navigates back finds it already there |
| **When it is cleared** | **On sign-out**, together with every other `fr.*` value; when a hold is acquired for a **different** showtime; and when the tab closes — `sessionStorage` has exactly the right lifetime and needs no expiry of its own (`P-HLD-09`) |
| **Present, and its `showtime_id` matches this route** | **Already confirmed.** Redirect to the confirmation screen for that reference |
| **Absent, or its `showtime_id` names another showtime** | **Expired.** The hold ended without producing a booking; return to the seat map per the row above |

**The screen does not re-send the confirm to find out.** A replay of `EP-PAY-01` spends a rate-limit
token whether or not it creates anything — `P-XCT-07` exception 4 is explicit that a retry carrying an
already-seen `Idempotency-Key` still consumes one, and `EP-PAY-01`'s own `rate_limit` field says the
same — and it can answer `409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT`, or the stored `201`, or `409 HOLD_EXPIRED` when
no booking was ever made. **That is three outcomes to disambiguate in order to answer a question the
client already knows the answer to**, and it spends a token from a bucket the customer may need for a
real retry.

**Sign-out clears it, and that is the clause that matters most on a shared device.** Signing out
clears **every** `fr.*` value in `sessionStorage` — the pending selection (`P-ACC-13`), the hold token
and its `Idempotency-Key` (`P-HLD-09`), and `fr.last_booking_reference`. The hold itself is released
at the same moment; lane E2 carries that as the `SIGN_OUT` input of the seat lifecycle machine.

**The consequence of omitting it is sharper than a stranded hold, and it is why this is stated rather
than assumed.** `sessionStorage` is scoped to the tab, not to the account. Customer A confirms a
booking, signs out, and hands the laptop over; customer B signs in **in the same tab** and opens
`/showtimes/{id}/checkout`. The rule above fires on a value that is still customer A's: **the screen
redirects — with no request, so nothing authenticates and nothing is checked — to customer A's
confirmation URL.** Customer B lands on a 404 for a booking that is not theirs, **with a stranger's
booking reference in their address bar.** The reference is the only proof of purchase in this product
and the only thing that gets someone through the door (`OPEN-EMAILFAIL-01`), so leaking one into
another person's history is not a cosmetic defect. **Clearing on sign-out is what makes the
no-request redirect safe**, and the two rules may not be separated: anything that makes this screen
act on a stored value without a request depends on that value belonging to whoever is signed in now.

**Why the reference and not the idempotency key.** The key identifies a *request*; the reference
identifies the *booking*. A stored key tells the screen only that a confirm was once attempted, which
is also true of an attempt that failed — so it cannot distinguish the two states, which is the whole
job. The reference exists only if a booking exists.

**States.**

| State | What renders |
|---|---|
| **Empty** | Cannot occur with a valid hold — a hold holds at least one seat. If the route is reached with no hold token in `sessionStorage`, the screen redirects to the seat map for that showtime and renders nothing of the panel. |
| **Loading** (arriving, prices not yet in hand) | Panel at full height. Seat lines render as `--fr-surface-inset` blocks. The total is absent. The pay action is present and disabled. The panel never blanks and never collapses, because a panel that changes height moves the pay action under a thumb. |
| **Ready** | Notice slab, heading, showtime line, seat lines with prices, perforation, total, countdown, pay action enabled. |
| **In flight** (payment running) | The pay action shows a busy state and is disabled. **The countdown keeps running. Nothing else on the panel moves.** The panel does not blank and the seat lines do not reflow. |
| **Success** | The screen writes `fr.last_booking_reference` to `sessionStorage` from the `201` body, then navigates to the confirmation screen for the new booking (lane E4, `FR-ADR-048`). The write happens before the navigation, so a customer who comes straight back finds it. This screen writes no confirmation copy of its own. |
| **Error** | The banner renders above the panel with the copy in the table below, and the panel stays exactly as it was so the customer can see what they were buying. The pay action re-enables unless the state below says otherwise. |
| **Partial** | Some seat prices known, some not: the seat lines that are known render, the total is absent, and the pay action is disabled. A partial total is a wrong number. |
| **Last 60 seconds** | The countdown digits and bar switch to `--fr-countdown-urgent` and the warning line appears. The change is announced once through a live region. Nothing else changes. |
| **Expired** (`0:00`) | The countdown stops at `0:00`. The pay action is disabled. The component states that the hold has expired and **does not claim the seats are free** — the server owns that. The customer is returned to the seat map with their previous selection re-applied and the map refreshed (`FR-ADR-047`). |
| **Already confirmed** (the customer navigates back to this route after succeeding) | `fr.last_booking_reference` is present in `sessionStorage` for this showtime. The screen redirects to the confirmation screen for that reference and **issues no request**. It does not re-present a pay action for a booking that already exists. |
| **Receipt state** | Nothing renders here about the receipt. The email is asynchronous and this screen makes no claim about it (`FR-ADR-048`, lane E4). |

**Copy.** Every string a customer reads on this screen.

| Where | Verbatim |
|---|---|
| Notice slab | "No real payment is taken. This is a demonstration system. Nothing is charged and no card details are collected." |
| Heading | "Confirm your booking" |
| Total label | "TOTAL" |
| Pay action | "Pay ₹1,661.46" — the current total, formatted with Indian digit grouping |
| Pay action, busy | "Confirming…" |
| Pay action, disabled because the hold expired | "Hold expired" |
| Secondary action | "Back to seats" |
| Countdown label | **Rendered from `SCR-SEA-02` (lane E2). Not restated here** — see the note below the table |
| Countdown warning line, last 60 seconds | **Rendered from `SCR-SEA-02` (lane E2). Not restated here** |
| Countdown at zero, no confirm in flight | **Rendered from `SCR-SEA-02` (lane E2). Not restated here** |
| Countdown at zero, a confirm in flight | **Rendered from `SCR-SEA-02` (lane E2). Not restated here** |
| `AUTH_REQUIRED` | "Sign in to complete this booking." |
| `HOLD_EXPIRED` | **Rendered from `P-HLD-14` (lane E2), its *at confirm* row. Not restated here** — see the note below the table |
| `HOLD_NOT_OWNED` | **Rendered from `P-HLD-14` (lane E2), its *at confirm* row. Not restated here** |
| `SEAT_UNAVAILABLE` | **Rendered from `P-HLD-14`, its *at confirm* rows 4 and 4b — the singular at one lost seat, the plural at two or more. Not restated here.** **The screen substitutes nothing**: the server renders the complete sentence with every seat already named in it (`SCR-XCT-01`), and this screen displays `message` as received. `details.unavailable_seats` is read only to mark those seats on the map behind the panel, never to compose the words |
| `PAYMENT_FAILED` | "The payment did not go through and you have not been charged. Your seats are still held - the time left is shown above. You can try again." **when the hold survived**, and "The payment did not go through and you have not been charged. The hold on your seats has also ended and they have been released. Choose them again if they are still free." **when it did not** — the server knows which, because the confirm re-validates the hold, and one unconditional sentence would be false in the second case. **Published once by `P-PAY-01` exception 4, which owns both strings. Not restated here** — and not `P-HLD-14`'s, which carries no `PAYMENT_FAILED` row. |
| `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT` | "This booking is still being processed." |
| `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` | "This checkout is out of date. Return to the seat map and choose your seats again." |
| `REQUEST_INVALID` | "This request could not be processed. Return to the seat map and choose your seats again." |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | "Too many attempts. Try again in 6 seconds." — the number comes from `Retry-After` and is rendered by **S7.20**; the screen formats nothing itself. `P-PAY-01` exception 7 owns the sentence and carries the arithmetic |
| `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` | **Rendered from `P-HLD-14` (lane E2), its *at confirm* row. Not restated here** |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | "Something went wrong and your booking was not completed. No payment was taken. If you need help, quote `a1b2c3d4`." — the request id comes from the error envelope and is shown on 5xx only |

**No error banner on this screen carries a control, and `HOLD_EXPIRED` is the case worth naming.**
`SCR-XCT-01` publishes a `Choose seats again` banner action against `HOLD_EXPIRED`. **That action is
for surfaces that are neither the seat map nor this screen.** Here the return is already automatic —
the **Expired** state above returns the customer to the seat map with their previous selection
re-applied and the map refreshed (`FR-ADR-047`) — so a button offering to do the thing that is already
happening is a control with nothing to do, and a customer who presses it during the navigation
presses a control that has left the screen. `SCR-SEA-03` reaches the same answer for the seat map for
the neighbouring reason — **a customer meeting `HOLD_EXPIRED` there is already on the screen the
button would send them to.** Two screens, one surface each, the same conclusion, and the
cross-cutting registry defers to both by name. **This screen's banner is text and a request id line;
it has no action slot, and that is specified rather than merely unmentioned.**

**The countdown's four rows are deferred, and this screen publishes no countdown copy at all.**
`SCR-SEA-02` declares itself "the single source for this component's label and its states" and says in
terms that the checkout screen's countdown is a **repetition of that component, not a second one**,
and that this lane specifies no label, no state and no wording for it. This screen previously
published a shortened warning line — *"At 0:00 your seats are released and you will need to choose
them again."* against `SCR-SEA-02`'s *"Less than a minute left. At 0:00 your seats are released and
you will need to choose them again."* — which is exactly the variant `SCR-SEA-02` calls a defect in
the other document. **It is deleted rather than reconciled**, because publishing a matching copy here
would leave two strings to keep in step and the next edit would separate them again. A developer
implementing this screen reads all four countdown strings out of `SCR-SEA-02` and nowhere else.

**The four deferred error rows.** `HOLD_EXPIRED`, `HOLD_NOT_OWNED`, `SEAT_UNAVAILABLE` and
`DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` are E2's copy, published as one set in `P-HLD-14` with a row for each marked
*at confirm*. **This screen renders those strings; it does not own them and it does not carry a second
copy of them**, because two copies in two lanes drift and these four already had (`P-PAY-01`). A
developer implementing this screen reads the four strings out of `P-HLD-14` and nowhere else. Every
other row in the table above is this screen's own and is specified here.

No apology, no exclamation mark, no figure of speech, and **no sentence that blames the customer for a
race they lost** (`SRC-002 §2.2`, `FR-ADR-052`). That rule governs the strings this screen owns; the
four it renders from `P-HLD-14` are held to the same rule there, and "someone beat you to it" is
forbidden in both places.

**Accessibility.**

- **Focus order** follows visual order: notice slab (as a landmark, not a control) → heading → seat
  lines → total → countdown → pay action → back to seats. The error banner, when it arrives, is
  inserted before the panel in the DOM so it precedes the panel in focus order as well.
- **Focus ring** is `--fr-stroke-bold` solid `--fr-focus-ring` with `outline-offset: 2px`, never
  removed and never replaced by a shadow (`COMPONENTS.md §0.2`).
- **Accessible names.** The pay action's accessible name includes the amount: "Pay 1,661 rupees 46
  paise". The countdown has an accessible name of "Seats held for 2 minutes 14 seconds", updated at a
  granularity that does not flood a screen reader — the live region announces only the 60-second
  threshold and the zero state, not every tick.
- **Live regions.** The error banner is announced through an assertive live region; an error that is
  only red has not been reported (`FR-ADR-051`). The 60-second warning and the expiry are announced
  once each through a polite live region.
- **Target size.** The pay action and the back action are at least `--fr-tap-min` tall.
- **The notice slab is not a control.** It has no dismiss affordance to reach, because it cannot be
  dismissed.
- **Motion.** The banner arrives over `--fr-motion-base` with `--fr-ease-out`, and collapses under
  `prefers-reduced-motion`. No motion on this screen carries information.

## S5 / E4 — The receipt, the reference and entry

#### `SCR-TKT-01` · Booking confirmation and receipt page
**Route.** `/bookings/{reference}` · **Who reaches it.** the signed-in owner of the booking, and nobody
else — **there is no admin override** (`P-TKT-09`). A guest cannot reach it. · **Component basis.**
`COMPONENTS.md §9` (the booking reference), `§6` (the error banner), `§0.1`–`§0.6` (the foundations)

**What the user arrives with / leaves with.** They arrive either straight from a successful confirm
(lane E3) or from their bookings list (lane E5) or by typing the URL. They leave with the reference,
the seats, the hall, the showtime, the film and the amount paid — everything the receipt would have
carried. **This page is durable and reachable again, not a one-time interstitial. A customer who
closes it has lost nothing** (`FR-ADR-048`).

**There is one booking page in this product and this is it.** `/bookings/{reference}` is reached from
three places and only three: the confirm response, which lane E3 navigates here on success
(`P-TKT-03`); the account lane's bookings **list**, `SCR-ACC-04`, whose rows link here; and a typed or
pasted URL. **The bookings list is a list. It links to this page and does not restate it, and there is
no second booking-detail screen anywhere in the product.** Two screens claiming to be the durable
booking page is how two reference blocks and two different not-found sentences come to exist, which is
exactly what had happened before the merge pass.

**This specification is the single source for everything this page says**, including its not-found
wording — `No booking with that reference is on your account.` — its reference block, and every string
in the copy table below. Copy written for this route in any other section is superseded by this one,
and a change to any of it is made here.

**Fields and controls.**

| Element | Token(s) | Behaviour | Validation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Page frame | `--fr-surface-base`, `--fr-page-max`, gutter `--fr-space-4` / `--fr-space-6` | standard frame; the body never scrolls horizontally | — |
| Confirmation heading | `--fr-font-display`, `--fr-text-xl`, `--fr-ink-strong`, `--fr-leading-tight` | receives focus on arrival | — |
| Reference block container | `--fr-surface-inset`, `--fr-radius-md`, padding `--fr-space-4` | the loudest thing on the page | — |
| Reference | `--fr-font-mono`, `--fr-text-2xl`, `--fr-weight-bold`, `--fr-ink-strong`, `letter-spacing: var(--fr-track-ref)` | rendered `FR-XXXX-XXXX`; the hyphens are presentation | — |
| Perforation above and below the reference | dashed `--fr-stroke-hair` `--fr-rule`, `--fr-space-4` clear | separates the reference from the prose | — |
| Reference label | `--fr-text-xs`, `--fr-ink-muted`, uppercase, `--fr-track-caps` | reads "BOOKING REFERENCE" | — |
| Copy control | `--fr-accent-ink`, `--fr-text-sm`, hit area at least `--fr-tap-min` | copies the eight characters with the `FR-` prefix and hyphens; announces success in a live region | — |
| Booking facts list | labels `--fr-text-xs` / `--fr-ink-muted` / `--fr-track-caps`; values `--fr-font-mono` / `--fr-text-md` / `--fr-ink` | film, hall, showtime, seats, amount paid. **Seats render in the order `EP-TKT-01` returns them** — row letter, then seat number as an integer (`E5 P-ACC-10`) — and the screen never re-sorts | — |
| Amount paid | `--fr-font-mono`, `tabular-nums` | rendered from integer paise at render time, Indian grouping (`FR-ADR-036`) | — |
| Row divider | `--fr-rule-quiet` | cosmetic only | — |
| Resend control | `--fr-accent-ink`, `--fr-text-sm`, hit area at least `--fr-tap-min` | calls `EP-TKT-02`; disabled while a request is in flight | rate limited server-side; the button is never the enforcement point |
| Error banner | `COMPONENTS.md §6` tokens | appears above the facts, announced in a live region | branches on `code`, never on message text (`FR-ADR-052`) |

**States.**

| State | What renders |
|---|---|
| **Empty** | Not reachable. This page always has a booking or it is a 404. There is no empty variant, and one must not be invented. |
| **Loading** | The frame, the heading and `--fr-surface-inset` blocks the size of the reference block and each fact row. The reference is never rendered as a placeholder string — a fake reference on this page is the one thing a customer might copy down. |
| **Error — 404** | The reference block is not rendered. The error banner renders: "No booking with that reference is on your account." |
| **Error — 401** | The customer is sent to sign in, and returned to this URL afterwards. |
| **Error — 503** | The error banner renders: "This page is unavailable right now. Your booking is not affected." |
| **Error — 5xx** | The error banner renders the generic message plus the request id line in `--fr-text-xs` / `--fr-ink-muted` / `--fr-font-mono` (`FR-ADR-052`). |
| **Success — first render after confirming** | Heading, reference block, facts, and the receipt sentence naming the address. This is the only state that mentions the email. **Entered when the confirm response is present in the client's navigation state, and by no other test** (`P-TKT-03`). |
| **Success — any later visit** | Heading, reference block, facts. **No sentence about the email in any form.** Not "sent", not "on its way", not "delayed". Omission, deliberately: see `P-TKT-03`. **This is the state a reload renders**, including a reload one second after confirming — the navigation state does not survive a page load, and the reference block, which is the thing that matters, renders identically in both. |
| **Partial — receipt queued or in flight** | Identical to the state above. Nothing changes. The reference is already the proof (`COMPONENTS.md §9`). |
| **Partial — receipt definitively failed** | **Not specified, and nothing may be written here.** `FR-ADR-049` is `NOT_DECIDED` and reserved (`OPEN-EMAILFAIL-01`). In v1 this state is indistinguishable on screen from the state above, because the dispatch state is not on the customer API (`P-TKT-09`). |
| **Resend accepted** | A live-region line: "A receipt was requested. It will arrive at `<address>`." The reference block does not change. |
| **Resend refused — the first receipt has not been attempted** | A live-region line: "The first receipt has not been sent yet. Wait for it to arrive before requesting another." Nothing was enqueued and no rate-limit token was spent, so the control stays available (`P-TKT-07` exception 3). |
| **Resend already in flight** | A live-region line: "A receipt is already being sent for this booking." |
| **Resend rate limited — the per-booking interval** | The error banner: "A receipt was requested recently. You can request another in 4 minutes." The number is substituted from `Retry-After` and rendered by `S7.20`'s rule; `300 − elapsed` is 240 at the worked instant, which is at or above the 120-second threshold, so it renders as minutes. |
| **Resend rate limited — the per-user lookup bucket** | The error banner: "Too many attempts. Try again in 3 seconds." A different bucket, a different figure and a different sentence: `ceil(60 / 20) = 3`. The interface branches on `Retry-After`, not on which words it expects (`FR-ADR-052`). |
| **Resend rate limited — the per-IP lookup bucket** | The error banner: "Too many attempts. Try again in 1 second." `ceil(60 / 60) = 1`, **singular**. Reached when several callers share one address, which is the case that refuses first. |
| **Resend refused — demonstration data** | The error banner: "This is demonstration data. No receipt was sent for this booking and none can be — the address is a placeholder, not a real inbox." Reachable only on a seeded booking, whose `receipt_dispatch` row is `suppressed` (`P-TKT-04`, `P-TKT-07` exception 8). **The control stays enabled** — no token was spent and there is nothing to wait for — and pressing it again produces the identical banner. |

**Copy.**

| Where | Verbatim |
|---|---|
| Heading | `Your booking is confirmed.` |
| Reference label | `BOOKING REFERENCE` |
| Receipt sentence — **first render only** | `A receipt is on its way to name@example.com.` |
| Entry line | `Show this reference at the entrance. A person will check it.` |
| Fact labels | `FILM` · `HALL` · `SHOWTIME` · `SEATS` · `PAID` |
| Copy control | `Copy reference` |
| Copy confirmation, live region | `Reference copied.` |
| Resend control | `Send the receipt again` |
| Resend accepted, live region | `A receipt was requested. It will arrive at name@example.com.` |
| Resend refused, first receipt not yet attempted | `The first receipt has not been sent yet. Wait for it to arrive before requesting another.` |
| Resend already in flight | `A receipt is already being sent for this booking.` |
| Resend rate limited, per-booking interval | `A receipt was requested recently. You can request another in 4 minutes.` |
| Resend rate limited, per-user lookup bucket | `Too many attempts. Try again in 3 seconds.` |
| Resend rate limited, per-IP lookup bucket | `Too many attempts. Try again in 1 second.` — **singular, and it ships** |
| Booking lookup rate limited, per-user bucket | `Too many attempts. Try again in 3 seconds.` |
| Booking lookup rate limited, per-IP bucket | `Too many attempts. Try again in 1 second.` — **singular, and it ships**; `S7.20` names this bucket as one of four in the product that reach `Retry-After: 1` |
| Resend refused, demonstration data | `This is demonstration data. No receipt was sent for this booking and none can be — the address is a placeholder, not a real inbox.` |

`FR-ADR-048` fixes the shape of the confirmation copy: the screen says what has actually happened, and
**"we have sent you an email" never appears**, because at that moment it is not true and it may not
become true. There is no apology, no exclamation mark and no figure of speech anywhere on this page
(`SRC-002 §2.2`).

**Accessibility.** On arrival, focus moves to the confirmation heading, which is the page's only `h1`.
Focus order then runs heading → reference → copy control → facts → resend control, matching visual
order. The reference element carries an accessible name that spells the characters separated by
spaces, so a screen reader reads `F R, A B C D, E F G H` character by character rather than attempting
a word. The copy confirmation, the resend outcomes and the error banner are announced through a live
region — an error that is only red has not been reported (`FR-ADR-051`). The copy and resend controls
have a hit area of at least `--fr-tap-min`. Every interactive element takes the standard focus ring
(`COMPONENTS.md §0.2`) and the ring is never removed.

#### `SCR-TKT-02` · The receipt email
**Route.** none — it is delivered, not navigated to · **Who reaches it.** the account's own email
address (`FR-ADR-014`); it is never sent to an address supplied in a request · **Component basis.**
`COMPONENTS.md §9` for the reference's role. **`tokens.css` does not apply here** — an email client
does not load the site's stylesheet, so this surface names no design token and uses no CSS custom
property. Naming one would be a claim that cannot be honoured.

**What the user arrives with / leaves with.** They arrive with nothing; they leave with the reference
and every fact needed at a door, without signing in.

**Fields and controls.**

| Element | Token(s) | Behaviour | Validation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sender address | none — `SES_SENDER_ADDRESS`, required, no default (`FR-ADR-060`) | whatever identity the client has verified in SES | the process refuses to start if it is unset (`FR-ADR-053`) |
| Sender display name | none | `FrontRow` | — |
| Subject | none | carries the reference so the customer can find the message by searching for it | — |
| Plain-text part | none | the authoritative part; every fact appears here | — |
| HTML part | none | the same content, minimal markup, no external resource of any kind | no remote image, no web font, no tracking pixel |
| Reference | none — a monospaced face is requested in the HTML part and is not guaranteed | rendered `FR-XXXX-XXXX` | re-formatted from the stored 8 characters at send time (`P-TKT-06`) |
| Link to the booking page | none | `<PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/bookings/FR-ABCD-EFGH`, from configuration. **In the plain-text part the URL stands on its own line after the sentence that introduces it; in the HTML part the anchor text is the published sentence below and never the bare URL**, because a URL read aloud by a screen reader is unusable and `Click here` names nothing | signing in is required to open it; the link carries no token |

**States.**

| State | What renders |
|---|---|
| **Empty** | Not applicable. An email is either sent complete or not sent. There is no partial receipt, and a receipt missing the hall is worse than a late one (`P-TKT-06` exception 1). |
| **Loading** | Not applicable. |
| **Error** | Not a state of this surface. A failed send renders nothing to anybody; it is recorded in `receipt_dispatch` (`P-TKT-05`) and is otherwise invisible (`P-TKT-11`). |
| **Success** | The message below, both parts. |
| **Partial** | Never. |
| **Re-sent** | Byte-identical content to the first send. A resend is not marked as a resend, because the facts have not changed and a customer holding two identical messages is not confused about which is real. |

**Copy.** Subject:

```
Your FrontRow booking FR-ABCD-EFGH
```

Plain-text body, verbatim, with the bracketed values substituted:

```
Your booking is confirmed.

Booking reference: FR-ABCD-EFGH

Film      DEMO MOVIE 01
Hall      Hall 3
Showtime  21 Aug 2026, 7:15 pm (Asia/Kolkata)
Seats     F7, F8, F9
Paid      Rs 843.72

Show this reference at the entrance. A person will check it.

You can see this booking again at https://example.invalid/bookings/FR-ABCD-EFGH

This booking is final. There is no cancellation and no refund.
```

**The link's anchor text, published because a control with no words is a defect** (`S1.2.1` case 3 —
no P-row publishes it, so this surface owns it): the HTML part renders
`See this booking again` as the anchor, on its own line, pointing at the same URL the plain-text part
prints in full. The two parts carry the same information in the shape each medium can use — a
text-only client needs the URL visible, and an HTML client needs words that say where the link goes.

**The `Showtime` line is `S7.19`'s date-with-time form followed by `(Asia/Kolkata)`.** This surface is
the one place in the product that prints the zone, because it is the one surface read outside the site
and possibly outside the zone (`S7.19` rule 2), and the year is never dropped on a receipt. The line
previously read `21 August 2026, 19:15 (Asia/Kolkata)`, which broke two rules — a month spelled in
full is not one of the five forms, and a 24-hour clock never reaches a customer.

The HTML part carries the same lines in the same order. **The last line is a statement of the ruled
position** (`SRC-003 OPEN-CANCEL-01`, `OPEN-CANCEL-02`, `FR-ADR-013`) and not a policy invented here.
The amount is written `Rs 843.72` in the plain-text part because the `₹` symbol renders unreliably in
plain-text mail clients; the HTML part uses `₹843.72`. There is no tax line, no fee line and no
discount line, and no space is left for one (`FR-ADR-040`).

**Accessibility.** The HTML part is a single-column document with real heading and list elements, no
layout tables, and no image — so it has no alternative text to get wrong. Every fact in the HTML part
is also in the plain-text part, which is what a customer reading with a screen reader or a text-only
client receives. The reference is on its own line in both parts so it can be read out without
surrounding prose.

## S5 / E5 — Accounts and the customer's own bookings

#### `SCR-ACC-01` · Sign in or register — one screen, two tabs
**Route.** `/sign-in` and `/register` — **two routes, one screen**, with the tab preselected by the
route. Switching tabs replaces the URL without a navigation, so the browser's back button returns to
the seat map rather than to the other tab.
· **Who reaches it.** guest · a customer whose session expired · anyone following a "sign in" control
· **Component basis.** `COMPONENTS.md §11` (forms), `COMPONENTS.md §6` (the error banner)

**What the user arrives with / leaves with.** They arrive from one of two places: the movie listing,
with nothing, or the seat map, having pressed "Sign in to hold these seats" — in which case
`fr.pending_selection` has already been written (`P-ACC-13`). Both are **deliberate** sign-ins. They
leave with a session cookie and are returned to exactly where they came from: the seat map for the
stored showtime, with the selection restored, or the movie listing.

**A third arrival exists and this screen does not own its destination**: a customer sent here by a
`401` mid-task. `SCR-XCT-04` preserves the path they were on and returns them there. The scope note
under the states table below sets out both cases and which row owns each.

**Fields and controls.**

| Element | Token(s) | Behaviour | Validation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tab bar — `Sign in` / `Register` | one row; `--fr-rule` under the unselected, `--fr-surface-accent` bar under the selected | two tabs, never two destinations (`FR-ADR-046`). The email field's contents survive a tab switch; the password field does not | — |
| Email field | `--fr-surface-inset`, 1px `--fr-control-edge`, `--fr-radius-md`, min height `--fr-tap-min`, text `--fr-ink` at `--fr-text-md` | `type="email"`, `autocomplete="email"`, `inputmode="email"` | shape checked on blur; **enforced on the server** (`P-ACC-01`) |
| Email label | `--fr-text-sm`, `--fr-weight-medium`, `--fr-ink` | always visible, never a placeholder | — |
| Password field | as the email field | `autocomplete="current-password"` on the sign-in tab, `new-password` on the register tab | length checked on blur on the register tab only; enforced on the server |
| Show-password control | `--fr-accent-ink`, `--fr-text-sm` | toggles the field between masked and visible; the accessible name changes with the state | — |
| Password help text | `--fr-text-xs`, `--fr-ink-muted` | **on the register tab, visible before the field is touched** — the rules are stated before they are broken (`P-ACC-03`) | — |
| Primary action | `--fr-surface-accent` fill, `--fr-ink-on-accent`, `--fr-radius-md`, min height `--fr-tap-min`, `--fr-weight-bold` | reads `Sign in` or `Create account` by tab | disabled only while a request is in flight, never while a field is invalid — a control that cannot be pressed cannot say why |
| Forgot-password link | `--fr-accent-ink`, `--fr-text-sm` | sign-in tab only; opens `SCR-ACC-02`, carrying whatever is in the email field | — |
| Context note | `--fr-text-sm`, `--fr-ink-muted` | shown only when `fr.pending_selection` exists: states that the seats are still selected | — |
| Field in error | border becomes 2px `--fr-danger-ink`; message `--fr-text-xs` `--fr-danger-ink` | associated with the field and announced, not only coloured (`FR-ADR-051`) | — |
| Form-level failure | `COMPONENTS.md §6` banner on `--fr-surface-danger` | used for `CREDENTIALS_INVALID`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE`, `INTERNAL_ERROR` | — |

**There is no "remember me" control**, no social sign-in, and no password-strength meter. None is asked
for by any source, and a strength meter would contradict `P-ACC-03`'s deliberate absence of composition
rules by scoring what the rules do not require.

**States.**

| State | What renders |
|---|---|
| **Empty** | The full form at full height, both fields blank, the primary action enabled. A form is its own empty state (`COMPONENTS.md §11`). |
| **Loading** | The primary action shows a busy state and is disabled. **Both fields stay readable and stay filled.** Nothing is blanked and nothing resizes. |
| **Error — field** | The offending field takes the 2px `--fr-danger-ink` border and its message renders beneath it, associated by `aria-describedby` and announced. Other fields keep their values. |
| **Error — form** | The banner renders above the tab bar. The password field is cleared; the email field is not. Clearing the password is so a shoulder-surfer does not read a failed attempt off a screen the customer has stopped looking at. |
| **Success** | No success screen. The interface navigates immediately: to the seat map with the selection restored if `fr.pending_selection` exists, otherwise to the movie listing. A success message on a screen nobody stays on is a screen nobody reads. **This rule governs a deliberate sign-in only — see the scope note below.** |
| **Partial** | Not applicable — there is nothing to load. The screen renders complete on first paint and needs no data fetch. |
| **Rate limited** | The banner states the wait, **rendered from the `Retry-After` integer by `S7.20`** — seconds below 120, minutes at or above it, so this screen's sign-in strings read "90 seconds" and "30 seconds" while its registration string reads "12 minutes". The header itself is never shown. The primary action stays enabled: the customer may try again, and the server is the thing that says no. |
| **Redis unavailable** | The banner states that sign-in is unavailable and that browsing still works. It never silently degrades (`FR-ADR-028`). |

**Copy.**

| Where | Verbatim |
|---|---|
| Tab labels | `Sign in` · `Register` |
| Email label | `Email address` |
| Password label | `Password` |
| Password help, register tab | `At least 12 characters. No numbers or symbols required. Maximum 72 bytes.` — **`12` interpolates `PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH`**; `72` is bcrypt's truncation point and is correctly a literal (`P-ACC-01`) |
| Primary action, sign-in tab | `Sign in` |
| Primary action, register tab | `Create account` |
| Forgot-password link | `I have forgotten my password` |
| Context note when a selection is pending | `Your seats are still selected. Sign in to hold them.` |
| Show-password control | `Show password` / `Hide password` |
| Invalid credentials | `That email address and password do not match an account.` |
| Email already registered | `An account already exists for that email address. Sign in instead, or reset the password if you have forgotten it.` |
| Email empty | `Enter an email address.` |
| Email malformed | `That is not a valid email address.` |
| Password too short | `Your password must be at least 12 characters. It does not have to contain numbers or symbols.` — **`12` interpolates `PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH`** |
| Password too long | `Your password is too long. The limit is 72 bytes and yours is 84. Most characters count as one byte; accented and non-Latin characters count as two, three or four.` |
| Rate limited, sign-in | `Too many sign-in attempts for that email address. Try again in 90 seconds.` |
| Redis unavailable | `Sign-in is unavailable right now. Browsing still works. Try again shortly.` |
| Unhandled failure | `Something went wrong and you were not signed in. If you need help, quote a1b2c3d4.` |

No sentence apologises, none uses an exclamation mark, and none blames the customer (`SRC-002 §2.2`,
`FR-ADR-052`).

**Which sign-in this screen's destination rule describes, and which it does not.**

This screen is reached two ways, and **its success destination governs only the first**:

| How the customer got here | Where sign-in sends them | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| **A deliberate sign-in** — they navigated here themselves, from the header or a link, with **no interrupted task to return to** | this screen's success rule above: the seat map if `fr.pending_selection` exists, otherwise the movie listing | **this screen** |
| **An interrupted request** — a `401` sent them here mid-task, from any surface | back to **the path they were on**, which `SCR-XCT-04` preserved | **`SCR-XCT-04`** |

**`SCR-XCT-04` owns the interrupted case, and this screen does not.** The 401 interstitial is the
surface the customer is actually on when the question arises, and it preserves **the path** rather than
only a seat selection — which is the difference that matters. Under this screen's rule applied to an
interruption, an admin whose session expired mid-edit has no `fr.pending_selection`, falls to
"otherwise", and is dropped on the movie listing with their work abandoned and no route back. A
manager interrupted on a dashboard lands there too. **The rule is right for the case it was written
for and wrong for the case it was being read into**, which is why the two are separated rather than
merged.

The two are **not one rule stated twice.** They take different inputs — a stored selection against a
preserved path — and they are correct for different situations, so a reader finding both has found a
deliberate pair.

**Accessibility.**

- Focus order: tab bar → email → password → show-password → primary action → forgot-password link.
  Visual order and focus order are the same (`FR-ADR-051`).
- The tab bar is a real tab pattern: `role="tablist"`, arrow keys move between tabs, and the panel is
  labelled by its tab. Switching tabs moves focus to the first field of the new panel.
- Every input has a programmatically associated visible label. No placeholder is used as a label.
- Field errors are associated with `aria-describedby` and the error region is a live region, so an
  error is announced and not only coloured (`FR-ADR-051`).
- The form-level banner is announced through the same live region as everywhere else in the product
  (`COMPONENTS.md §6`).
- Every control is at least `--fr-tap-min` tall.
- The focus ring is `--fr-stroke-bold` solid `--fr-focus-ring` with a 2px offset, never removed and
  never suppressed for mouse users (`COMPONENTS.md §0.2`).
- The show-password control's accessible name states the action it will perform, not the current state.

#### `SCR-ACC-02` · Request a password reset
**Route.** `/account/reset` · **Who reaches it.** anyone; normally from `SCR-ACC-01`'s
forgot-password link · **Component basis.** `COMPONENTS.md §11`

**What the user arrives with / leaves with.** They arrive with an email address they may have typed on
the previous screen, which is carried into the field. They leave having been told the same thing
whether or not the address has an account.

**Fields and controls.**

| Element | Token(s) | Behaviour | Validation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Email field | as `SCR-ACC-01` | `autocomplete="email"`; prefilled from the previous screen when available | shape only; enforced on the server (`P-ACC-07`) |
| Primary action | `--fr-surface-accent`, `--fr-ink-on-accent`, min height `--fr-tap-min` | reads `Send a reset link` | disabled only while in flight |
| Back link | `--fr-accent-ink`, `--fr-text-sm` | returns to `SCR-ACC-01` | — |
| Confirmation panel | `--fr-surface-raised`, `--fr-radius-lg`, padding `--fr-space-4`, text `--fr-ink` | replaces the form on `202` | — |

**States.**

| State | What renders |
|---|---|
| **Empty** | The form, one field, the action enabled. |
| **Loading** | The action is busy and disabled; the field stays filled and readable. |
| **Error** | Field-level for a malformed address; the `COMPONENTS.md §6` banner for `RATE_LIMITED`, `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE` and `INTERNAL_ERROR`. |
| **Success** | **The form is replaced by the confirmation panel**, which says the same words for a known and an unknown address. There is no second send control on this screen — a customer who sees "sent" and presses again would be told nothing new and would consume a bucket token. |
| **Partial** | Not applicable. |

**Copy.**

| Where | Verbatim |
|---|---|
| Heading | `Reset your password` |
| Body above the field | `Enter the email address on your account. If it has one, we will send a link that lets you set a new password.` |
| Email label | `Email address` |
| Primary action | `Send a reset link` |
| Confirmation panel | `If that email address has an account, a reset link is on its way to it. The link works once and expires in 30 minutes.` |
| Email empty or malformed | `Enter an email address.` |
| Rate limited | `Too many reset requests from this connection. Try again in 12 minutes.` |
| Dependency unavailable | `Password reset is unavailable right now. Try again shortly.` |
| Back link | `Back to sign in` |

**The `30` in the confirmation panel is rendered, not typed** (`P-ACC-07`). It is
`PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_SECONDS / 60` as a whole number of minutes, interpolated into the one shared
sentence that the `202` body and the reset email also use. A hard-coded `30` on this screen is a defect,
because the screen and the server would then be free to disagree about how long the link lives.

**Accessibility.** Focus order: email → primary action → back link. On success, focus moves to the
confirmation panel's heading and the panel is announced through a live region, because a customer using
a screen reader must be told the form was replaced rather than discover it by exploring.
